tools.name: add_animation_machine_state
tools.description: Append one state to the AnimationNodeStateMachine tree_root of the AnimationTree at 'animation_tree_path' (required string). Required 'state_name' (unique string, e.g. "idle"); optional 'animation' (animation name playable by that tree's player, e.g. "walk") assigned to the underlying AnimationNodeAnimation. Errors if tree_root is not a state machine or the state name exists. Returns the full 'states' list after insertion.

animation.description: Animation name assigned to the state's AnimationNodeAnimation, e.g. 'walk'

animation_tree_path.description: Path of the AnimationTree whose state machine root receives the state

state_name.description: Unique state name within the state machine, e.g. 'idle'

tools.name: add_audio_bus_effect
tools.description: Add a new audio effect to a bus. 'effect_type' must be the class name of an instantiable AudioEffect subclass, for example AudioEffectReverb or AudioEffectDistortion; unknown or abstract class names return an error. 'at_position' inserts the effect at that zero-based slot and defaults to -1, which appends at the end. Returns 'result' set to 'ok'.

at_position.description: Zero-based slot to insert the effect at; -1 (default) appends at the end

bus_index.description: Zero-based audio bus index; 0 is the Master bus

effect_type.description: Class name of an instantiable AudioEffect subclass, e.g. 'AudioEffectReverb' or 'AudioEffectDistortion'

tools.name: add_autoload
tools.description: Add a new autoload singleton to the project configuration. name must be unique (an existing autoload/Name setting is rejected) and must not contain '/'; path must be a res:// scene or script that loads and can be instantiated. enabled defaults to true and controls the leading * singleton marker, stored exactly like the editor writes it. The change is saved to project.godot immediately. Returns ok plus name, path, enabled and order.

enabled.description: Whether the singleton marker is stored; defaults to true, which writes the leading * marker exactly like the editor does

name.description: Autoload singleton name, e.g. Global; becomes the autoload/Name project setting and the node's name in the scene tree; must not exist yet and must not contain '/'.

path.description: res:// scene or script to autoload, e.g. res://global.gd; must exist, load and be instantiable

tools.name: add_editor_undo_redo_do
tools.description: Register a method call that runs when the undo/redo action is applied (the do step). Use it inside an action started with create_editor_undo_redo_action; target a node by node_path, name the method and pass an optional value argument. Pair it with add_editor_undo_redo_undo for the inverse, then finish with commit_editor_undo_redo. Returns result 'ok'.

method.description: Name of the node method to call, e.g. 'set_position' or 'queue_free'

node_path.description: Path to the node whose method will be called on redo, e.g. 'Player' or '/root/Player'; resolved against the edited scene root

value.description: Optional serialized JSON value passed as the single method argument; omit for methods without arguments

tools.name: add_editor_undo_redo_undo
tools.description: Register a method call that runs when the undo/redo action is reverted (the undo step). Use it to define the inverse of an operation added with add_editor_undo_redo_do; target a node by node_path, name the method and pass an optional value argument. Finish the action with commit_editor_undo_redo. Returns result 'ok'.

method.description: Name of the node method to call for the inverse operation, e.g. 'set_position'

node_path.description: Path to the node whose method will be called on undo, e.g. 'Player' or '/root/Player'; resolved against the edited scene root

value.description: Optional serialized JSON value passed as the single method argument; omit for methods without arguments

tools.name: add_group_node
tools.description: Add a scene node to a group persistently: the membership is saved with the scene and registered with the editor undo/redo. Requires 'node_path' and 'group_name'. Idempotent — if the node is already in the group it is removed first, then re-added. Returns 'added' with node_path, group and persistent.

group_name.description: Group name to add the node to (string, e.g. 'enemies')

node_path.description: Path to the scene node (string, e.g. 'Enemies/Enemy1')

tools.name: add_input_map_action
tools.description: Add a new empty input action to the editor project InputMap. 'deadzone' defaults to 0.5. Only the action is created; no events are bound, so use add_input_map_action_event to attach keys or buttons afterwards. The change modifies the editor project InputMap and persists to project settings; a running game process will not see the change until it restarts. Returns 'result' set to 'ok'.

action.description: Action name identifier, e.g. 'mario_jump' or 'move_left'; a programmatic identifier, not a display name

deadzone.description: Deadzone 0.0 to 1.0, the analog threshold below which input is ignored (default: 0.5)

tools.name: add_input_map_action_event
tools.description: Bind an input event to an action in the editor project InputMap. 'event' must be an object with a concrete 'class' field, for example InputEventKey with 'keycode' 65, or a KEY_* name string. The change modifies the editor project InputMap and persists to project settings; a running game process will not see the change until it restarts. Returns 'result' set to 'ok'.

action.description: Action name identifier to bind the event to, e.g. 'mario_jump'

event.description: Input event object with a concrete 'class' field, e.g. 'InputEventKey' with 'keycode' 65; keycode and physical_keycode accept numeric key codes or KEY_* names like 'KEY_A'

tools.name: add_physics_3d_body_collision_exception
tools.description: Add a collision exception to a 3D physics body so it stops colliding with another body. Requires rid and excepted_body_rid, both RIDs from create_physics_3d_body. The exception persists until removed with remove_physics_3d_body_collision_exception. Returns 'ok' or an error when either RID is invalid

excepted_body_rid.description: Required. RID id of the body to exclude from collision

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics body, e.g. from create_physics_3d_body

tools.name: add_physics_3d_body_shape
tools.description: Add a shape RID to a 3D physics body, giving it collision geometry. Requires rid of the body from create_physics_3d_body and shape_rid from create_physics_3d_sphere_shape; optional transform places the shape relative to the body, disabled starts it disabled (default false). Returns 'ok' or an error when either RID is invalid

disabled.description: Optional. True adds the shape disabled so it does not collide until re-enabled; default false

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics body, e.g. from create_physics_3d_body

shape_rid.description: Required. RID of the shape to attach, e.g. from create_physics_3d_sphere_shape

transform.description: Optional. Transform3D placing the shape relative to the body: object with basis (array of 3 row arrays) and origin (Vector3 object)

tools.name: add_render_canvas_item_circle
tools.description: Add a filled circle draw command to a canvas item. Pass the RID from create_render_canvas_item, a center position {x, y} and a color {r, g, b, a}; radius defaults to 1.0 and antialiased to false. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

canvas_item_rid.description: RID of the canvas item, from create_render_canvas_item

color.description: Fill color {r, g, b, a}, each in 0.0-1.0; example: {r: 1, g: 0, b: 0, a: 1}

tools.name: add_render_canvas_item_line
tools.description: Add a line draw command to a canvas item. Pass the RID from create_render_canvas_item, start point from, end point to and a color; width defaults to -1 (project setting) and antialiased to false. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

canvas_item_rid.description: RID of the canvas item, from create_render_canvas_item

color.description: Line color {r, g, b, a}, each in 0.0-1.0

from.description: Line start point {x, y}; example: {x: 0, y: 0}

to.description: Line end point {x, y}; example: {x: 100, y: 100}

width.description: Line width in pixels (default: -1.0, use project setting)

tools.name: add_render_canvas_item_rect
tools.description: Add a filled rectangle draw command to a canvas item. Pass the RID from create_render_canvas_item, a rect object {position: {x, y}, size: {x, y}} and a color object {r, g, b, a}; antialiased is optional and defaults to false. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

canvas_item_rid.description: RID of the canvas item, from create_render_canvas_item

color.description: Fill color {r, g, b, a}, each in 0.0-1.0; example: {r: 1, g: 0.5, b: 0, a: 1}

rect.description: Rectangle as {position: {x, y}, size: {x, y}}; example: {position: {x: 10, y: 20}, size: {x: 100, y: 50}}

tools.name: add_render_canvas_item_texture_rect
tools.description: Draw a texture inside a rectangle on a canvas item. Pass the RID from create_render_canvas_item, the texture RID from create_render_texture_from_image and a destination rect; tile, modulate and transpose are optional. Modulate tints the drawn texture. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

canvas_item_rid.description: RID of the canvas item, from create_render_canvas_item

modulate.description: Tint color {r, g, b, a}, each in 0.0-1.0; white leaves the texture unchanged

rect.description: Destination rectangle {position: {x, y}, size: {x, y}}; example: {position: {x: 0, y: 0}, size: {x: 100, y: 100}}

texture_rid.description: RID of the texture to draw, from create_render_texture_from_image

tile.description: Tile the texture inside the rect (default: false)

transpose.description: Swap the texture's x and y axes (default: false)

tools.name: add_render_mesh_surface
tools.description: Add a surface built from vertex arrays to a mesh. Pass the RID from create_render_mesh; primitive defaults to triangles and arrays may hold vertices, normals, tangents, colors, uvs and indices. Surfaces are indexed from 0 in call order. Returns 'ok'. Errors if mesh_rid is missing.

arrays.description: Surface arrays; keys: vertices and normals (arrays of {x, y, z} objects), tangents (flat array of floats, 4 per vertex), colors (array of {r, g, b, a} objects), uvs (array of {x, y} objects) and indices (array of integers)

mesh_rid.description: RID of the render mesh, from create_render_mesh

tools.name: add_shaped_text_string
tools.description: Add a text string to a shaped text object created by create_shaped_text. Requires shaped_rid (the RID id from create_shaped_text), text, font_rid (the RID id of a font configured with set_text_font_data) and size in pixels; optional language code improves shaping. Returns true on success as 'result'; run get_shaped_text_size afterwards to measure.

font_rid.description: RID id returned by create_text_font (configured with set_text_font_data first)

language.description: Language code (e.g. 'en', 'ar') to improve shaping; omit for auto detection

text.description: Text string to add (may contain Unicode)

tools.name: add_spriteframes_animation
tools.description: Add a named animation to a SpriteFrames resource created by create_spriteframes. Requires name (the memory:// reference) and animation; optional fps (default 5) and loop (default true) set playback behavior. Must run before add_spriteframes_frame targets the animation. The animation starts empty until frames are added. Returns 'ok'.

fps.description: Animation playback speed in frames per second (default: 5)

name.description: SpriteFrames name from create_spriteframes (memory:// reference)

tools.name: add_spriteframes_frame
tools.description: Add one or more frames to an animation of a SpriteFrames resource. Requires name (memory:// reference), animation (created first with add_spriteframes_animation) and texture path; optional duration (default 1.0). hframes and vframes (default 1) split a sprite sheet into per-cell AtlasTextures. Returns 'ok', frames (total count) and added_frames.

animation.description: Animation name to add the frame to (created with add_spriteframes_animation first)

hframes.description: Horizontal frame count for spritesheet splitting (default: 1; must be >= 1)

name.description: SpriteFrames name from create_spriteframes (memory:// reference)

texture.description: Texture file path (e.g. res://frame.png); must exist and import as Texture2D

vframes.description: Vertical frame count for spritesheet splitting (default: 1; must be >= 1)

tools.name: add_tilemap_atlas_source
tools.description: Add a TileSetAtlasSource with a texture to a TileSet created by create_tilemap_tileset. Requires name (the memory:// reference), source_id (0-255, must be unused), texture path and tile_size {x, y}; optional margin and spacing in pixels. Splits the texture into a grid and creates one tile per cell. Returns source_id, created_tiles and grid_size.

margin.description: Margin in pixels around the atlas texture (default: 0)

name.description: TileSet name from create_tilemap_tileset (memory:// reference)

source_id.description: Source ID to assign, 0-255; must not already be used

texture.description: Texture file path (e.g. res://tiles.png); must exist on disk

tools.name: add_tilemap_physics_layer
tools.description: Add a physics layer to a TileSet created by create_tilemap_tileset. Requires name (the memory:// reference) and layer_id; optional collision_layer and collision_mask bitmasks (default 1). Call it before set_tilemap_tile_collision, which needs an existing layer. Multiple layers add multiple collision polygons. Returns 'ok' and the actual layer_id.

layer_id.description: Physics layer index to add (appended at the end of the layer list)

name.description: TileSet name from create_tilemap_tileset (memory:// reference)

tools.name: advance_path_follow
tools.description: Advance a PathFollow2D/PathFollow3D node along its parent path curve by 'offset' pixels (negative moves backward). Requires 'path' (the follower node path in the edited scene) and 'offset' (number). Sets progress to current progress plus offset and reports the new progress, progress_ratio and global position. Marks the scene modified.

offset.description: Distance in pixels to advance along the curve; negative values move backward

path.description: Node path of a PathFollow2D/PathFollow3D in the edited scene (e.g. 'EnemyPath/Follower')

tools.name: apply_physics_2d_body_force
tools.description: Apply a continuous force to a 2D physics body, accelerating it while the force is applied. Requires rid and force (Vector2 with x and y); optional position offsets the force to a specific point, while omitting it applies a central force through the center of mass. Only affects bodies in rigid modes. Returns 'ok' or an error when the body RID or force is missing

force.description: Required. Force vector as a Vector2 object with x and y fields; applied to the center of mass when position is omitted

position.description: Optional. Force application point as a Vector2 object with x and y fields; omitting it applies a central force

rid.description: Required. RID of the 2D physics body, e.g. from create_physics_2d_body

tools.name: apply_physics_2d_body_impulse
tools.description: Apply an instantaneous impulse to a 2D physics body, causing an immediate change in velocity. Requires rid and impulse (Vector2 with x and y); optional position applies the impulse off-center, which adds rotation, while omitting it applies a central impulse. Use this for single quick events such as jumps or hits instead of apply_physics_2d_body_force. Returns 'ok' or an error for missing parameters

impulse.description: Required. Impulse vector as a Vector2 object with x and y fields; applied to the center of mass when position is omitted

position.description: Optional. Impulse application point as a Vector2 object with x and y fields; off-center impulses add rotation

rid.description: Required. RID of the 2D physics body, e.g. from create_physics_2d_body

tools.name: apply_physics_3d_body_force
tools.description: Apply a continuous force to a 3D physics body, accelerating it while the force is applied. Requires rid and force (Vector3 with x, y and z); optional position offsets the force to a specific point, while omitting it applies a central force through the center of mass. Only affects bodies in rigid modes. Returns 'ok' or an error when the body RID or force is missing

force.description: Required. Force vector as a Vector3 object with x, y and z fields; applied to the center of mass when position is omitted

position.description: Optional. Force application point as a Vector3 object with x, y and z fields; omitting it applies a central force

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics body, e.g. from create_physics_3d_body

tools.name: apply_physics_3d_body_impulse
tools.description: Apply an instantaneous impulse to a 3D physics body, causing an immediate change in velocity. Requires rid and impulse (Vector3 with x, y and z); optional position applies the impulse off-center, adding rotation, while omitting it applies a central impulse. Use this for single quick events such as jumps or hits instead of apply_physics_3d_body_force. Returns 'ok' or an error for missing parameters

impulse.description: Required. Impulse vector as a Vector3 object with x, y and z fields; applied to the center of mass when position is omitted

position.description: Optional. Impulse application point as a Vector3 object with x, y and z fields; off-center impulses add rotation

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics body, e.g. from create_physics_3d_body

tools.name: apply_physics_3d_body_torque
tools.description: Apply a rotational torque to a 3D physics body, spinning it around the given axis. Requires rid and torque (Vector3 with x, y and z), where each component sets rotation around that axis. Only affects bodies in rigid modes; there is no 2D counterpart because 2D rotation is scalar. Returns 'ok' or an error for missing parameters

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics body, e.g. from create_physics_3d_body

torque.description: Required. Torque vector as a Vector3 object with x, y and z fields; each component rotates the body around that axis

tools.name: apply_theme_to_control
tools.description: Assign a .tres theme file to a Control node in the edited scene. Requires theme_path (the .tres to load) and control_path (node path inside the current scene). Only the in-memory scene changes — call save_editor_scene afterwards to persist the assignment. Returns ok with control_path and theme_path.

control_path.description: Path of the Control node in the edited scene receiving the theme; only the in-memory scene changes — call save_editor_scene afterwards to persist

theme_path.description: Path of the .tres theme file to assign

tools.name: assign_collision_shape
tools.description: Assign a Shape resource to a CollisionShape node in the edited scene. Required 'node_path' is a CollisionShape2D or CollisionShape3D node; other node types fail with the actual class. Required 'shape_ref' is the shape to assign: an object_id integer from create_collision_shape, a res:// or memory:// string, or {"path": "res://..."} / {"resource": "memory://..."} / {"object_id": ...} / {"object_id_str": ...} / {"name": ...}. Memory:// resources are rejected because they are not persistent: save them first with save_resource to a res:// path and pass that path instead. The resource must match the node dimension: Shape2D for CollisionShape2D and Shape3D for CollisionShape3D, otherwise the actual class is reported. Only the in-memory scene changes, call save_editor_scene afterwards to persist. Returns ok with assigned, node_path, shape_class, object_id and undo info.

node_path.description: Required. Scene path of a CollisionShape2D or CollisionShape3D node in the edited scene; other node types fail with the actual class

shape_ref.description: Required. Shape resource reference: an object_id integer from create_collision_shape, a res:// or memory:// string, or {"path": "res://..."} / {"resource": "memory://..."} / {"object_id": ...} / {"object_id_str": ...} / {"name": ...}; memory:// resources are rejected, save them first with save_resource and pass the res:// path. Must be a Shape2D for CollisionShape2D and a Shape3D for CollisionShape3D, otherwise the actual class is reported

tools.name: assign_mesh_to_instance
tools.description: Assign a mesh to a MeshInstance2D or MeshInstance3D node in the edited scene. Requires node_path (scene-relative path such as 'Level/Enemy' or absolute '/root/Level/Enemy') and mesh_ref (memory://name string, bare registration name, res:// path, decimal object_id string, or locator object). Nodes of any other class are rejected with their actual class name. Returns ok with assigned, node_path, mesh_ref and class; a mesh without normals yields a shading warning. When the instance rejects the in-memory mesh, save it with save_resource first and assign the saved res:// path instead.

mesh_ref.description: Mesh locator: memory://name string, bare registration name, res:// path, decimal object_id string, or {name|path|object_id|resource} object

node_path.description: Scene-relative path to a MeshInstance2D or MeshInstance3D node, e.g. 'Level/Enemy' or absolute '/root/Level/Enemy'

tools.name: attach_script_to_node
tools.description: Attach a Script resource (e.g. a .gd file or another Script) to a node in the edited scene, registered with the editor undo/redo. Requires node_path and script_path. The script is always re-read from disk (CACHE_MODE_IGNORE) before attaching, so a node never receives a stale cached instance after the file changed outside the editor. Returns 'script attached to <path>' plus instantiated. When the script lacks @tool it cannot be instantiated in the editor, so its methods only run once the game runs — call_script_node reports the same restriction. Replacing an existing script does not migrate exported references (node_paths may be left dangling) — rewire them after attaching.

node_path.description: Node path in the edited scene to attach the script to. The response includes scene_path and scene_unsaved to confirm which scene was written

script_path.description: Resource path of a Script resource (e.g. a .gd file or another Script); the resource must be a Script

tools.name: build_csharp_assembly
tools.description: Trigger a C# project build with dotnet build --nologo on the res:// root .csproj/.sln. The engine path is globalized to an OS absolute path (ProjectSettings.globalize_path) before it reaches dotnet, because dotnet cannot resolve res:// paths. Intended for CI/command-line compile verification only: it does NOT rewind to an in-editor Build and does not hot-reload the loaded .NET assembly. By default (wait omitted or false) it launches via OS.create_process and returns immediately with result {project_file,project_path,command,pid,started,note}. With wait=true it runs synchronously via OS.execute, temporarily pinning DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE=en for the child process and restoring the previous value afterwards so that output_digest carries ASCII English text instead of ACP-mangled localized output, and waits for the BuildResult {project_file,project_path,command,exit_code,success,errors,output_digest,output_empty}: project_file is the res:// project file, project_path the OS absolute path handed to dotnet, command the logical dotnet invocation on the res:// file, exit_code the dotnet exit code, success exit_code==0, errors lists output lines containing error (capped at 50 with errors_truncated), output_digest the combined stdout/stderr truncated to 4000 chars when desensitized else 64000 chars with output_truncated when cut, output_empty true when nothing was captured (output_hint then explains the exit code); timeout_ms declares the wait budget (1-25000, default 25000) validated to stay below the dispatch default 27000ms; errors when the project is not a C# project or dotnet is not available. Both shapes also return next_action (array of executable follow-up steps), restart_required (true when the build succeeded or was launched, independent of whether a game is running, because nothing hot-reloads the loaded assemblies) and game_running. With probe_script the response additionally carries editor_assembly_probe {path,is_dotnet_editor,state,can_instantiate,base_class,hint}: the editor loads the .cs resource without instantiating it, state is 'available' when it loads and 'unavailable' with unavailable=true when the editor is not a .NET build or the load fails; can_instantiate=false on an available probe means the editor still runs the old assembly, so click Build or restart the editor.

probe_script.description: Optional res:// path ending in .cs, e.g. 'res://scripts/Player.cs'; after the build the editor loads this C# script (no instantiation) and reports result.editor_assembly_probe {path,is_dotnet_editor,state,can_instantiate,base_class,hint}; state is 'available' when the script resource loads and 'unavailable' with unavailable=true when the editor is not a .NET build or the load fails (E-11)

timeout_ms.description: Declared wait budget in milliseconds for wait=true only, an integer between 1 and 25000 (default 25000); validated to stay below the dispatch default 27000ms and the transport timeout; rejected when wait is not true

wait.description: When true run dotnet build synchronously via OS.execute and wait for the BuildResult with exit_code, success, errors and output_digest; when false or omitted launch via OS.create_process and return immediately with pid and started

tools.name: build_nodes_from_spec
tools.description: 用声明式 spec 一次建好整棵子树：传 'spec' 对象 {type（Node 子类，默认 Node）、name（默认 Node，'/' 与 ':' 非法）、props（经 property_set 同转换链逐节点应用，OBJECT 型值先行）、children（同形 spec 数组递归）}；可选 'parent_path'（默认场景根，仅在无场景时省略并让顶层 spec 节点成根）、'dry_run'/'preview'（任一 true 则只校验并返回节点清单，不写场景）。自顶向下挂接并设 owner 为场景根以保证落盘；任一步失败整体回滚（摘除顶层已建节点并释放子树，无残留）。递归上限 32 层、单次上限 500 节点。与 create_scene_node、code_execute 并存：定型结构用本工具，单次零散节点用 create_scene_node，异形逻辑（循环、条件、计算值）用 code_execute。返回 mode（built/dry_run）、node_count、created [{path, type}] 与 delete_scene_node 撤销提示。

dry_run.description: Validate the spec and return the node list without writing to the scene (default: false); either dry_run or preview enables preview-only mode

parent_path.description: Parent node path for the top spec node (default: scene root); omit only while the scene has no root, in which case the top spec node becomes the root

preview.description: Alias of dry_run: validate and preview without writing (default: false)

spec.description: Declarative subtree spec {type, name, props, children}: type is a Node subclass (default: Node), name must not contain '/' or ':' (default: Node), props maps property names to values applied through the property_set conversion chain with OBJECT-typed values applied first, children is an array of nested specs; recursion is capped at 32 levels and 500 nodes per call and any failure rolls the whole subtree back

tools.name: call_scene_tree_group
tools.description: Act on the running game process's SceneTree over the runtime channel — requires a game launched from the editor whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension, and game_runtime authorization. Unlike editor scene tools, this never touches the editor's own scene tree: without a running game it returns a structured error. Call a method on every node belonging to a group in that game SceneTree. Requires 'group_name' and 'method'; optional 'arguments' (array) is passed to the call. Returns 'ok' only — call_group collects no return values, so this confirms the call was dispatched rather than reporting per-node results.

arguments.description: Optional arguments array passed to the method (array, e.g. [10, 'fire'])

group_name.description: Name of the group whose nodes receive the call (string, e.g. 'enemies')

method.description: Method name to call on every group node (string, e.g. 'take_damage')

tools.name: call_script_node
tools.description: Call a method on a node in the edited scene. Requires node_path and function; optional args array passes arguments. The node's script must be marked @tool to run in the editor, otherwise the call errors — run the game instead for non-tool scripts. Unlike execute_script it runs inside the existing node instance; unlike execute_game_script it cannot reach the running game process.

function.description: Method name to call; the node's script must be @tool to run in the editor

node_path.description: Node path in the edited scene

tools.name: capture_display_screen
tools.description: Capture the contents of a physical screen as a PNG image. Use it to take desktop screenshots or verify window placement visually. Takes screen (default 0). Returns result with mime, format and data fields, where data is a base64-encoded PNG. Unlike capture_editor_viewport (editor viewport) and capture_game_viewport (running game), this tool captures the whole physical display.

screen.description: Index of the physical screen to capture, default 0; valid range is 0 to count-1 from get_display_screen_count

tools.name: capture_editor_viewport
tools.description: Capture a viewport as a PNG image and return it inline as base64 (image content). target='editor' (default) grabs the editor 2D viewport with a fallback to the 3D viewport; use it to visually verify the scene while editing, e.g. after placing nodes or changing properties. Optional 'space' picks what the editor target captures: 'viewport' (default) keeps the 2D viewport with 3D fallback behaviour, while 'window' grabs the editor main window root viewport exactly as shown on screen - docks, toolbars and the 2D grid/selection overlays included. The optional 'region' object {x, y, width, height} crops the captured image to that rectangle (width and height must be positive; the rect is clamped to the image, an empty intersection fails with code region_out_of_bounds), and optional 'max_dimension' (64-4096) downscales the result so its longest side is at most that many pixels; it never upscales. Both parameters apply to both targets: for target='game' the crop and downscale run inside the game process. They operate on the returned output image: the result reports the clamped 'region' when one was applied, source_width/source_height whenever the output was cropped or upscaled/downscaled, and width/height (plus 'space' on the editor target) for the final image. Optional 'scale' (integer 1-8, default 1) nearest-neighbour upscales the image after the crop and before 'max_dimension', so the cap still wins when both are given and width/height report the final size. For target='game', optional 'after_frames' (integer >= 0) waits that many rendered frames and optional 'when' (a GDScript expression re-evaluated every rendered frame against the current scene) holds the capture until the expression is true - together they capture short-lived feedback such as a 2 s banner or a 0.7 s death screen without slowing the game: act first, then capture with a condition; the condition holds on the rendered frame reported as when_satisfied_frame and the image is read on the next rendered frame (captured_frame > when_satisfied_frame), so the picture shows the state after the condition became true; a malformed expression fails immediately with a structured error (code when_parse_error) carrying the Expression error text, and a condition that never becomes true ends in a structured error (code when_timeout, plus frames_waited) bounded by 'timeout_ms' instead of hanging. target='editor' rejects 'after_frames'/'when' because the editor capture runs synchronously on the main thread. Optional 'diff_against_last' (default false) adds a 'diff' object comparing the final image with the previous editor capture: comparable plus changed_ratio and, when anything changed, changed_bbox; when the two sizes differ it compares the shared top-left region instead and additionally reports size_mismatch=true and current_size {x, y} next to baseline_size; when the images cannot be compared it returns comparable=false with a reason (no_baseline, unsupported_format or baseline_too_large). Optional 'annotate' (default false) draws numbered red boxes around UI controls and adds an 'elements' array (id, path, type, text, position, size) in final-image pixels whose ids match the box numbers, plus 'elements_truncated' when the 200-element cap was hit. It applies to both targets: the editor target annotates editor UI controls (window-level controls with space='window'), while target='game' annotates Controls of the running game inside the game process and returns the same elements table. Editor captures are not written to disk by default; pass save=true to also write the PNG under user://godot_autopilot/captures/ and receive its 'path' in the result, which also deletes the older gda_capture PNGs beyond the 20 most recent. target='game' captures the running game's root window over the runtime channel and returns data, format, width and height plus the absolute path of the PNG in the OS cache directory, along with region/source_width/source_height when the game applied them; it requires a game launched from the editor (play_editor_current_scene) whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension. Both targets keep only the 20 most recent gda_capture PNG files. Optional 'timeout_ms' applies to target='game' only (default: 5000, max: 30000). Write-tier tool (side_effect writes_file): save=true writes and prunes files under user://, and target='game' always writes a PNG in the game process; in strict mode without 'write' in the allow list the call is rejected with code authorization_required before any capture happens. Optional save/save_dir now apply to both targets: save=true (or giving save_dir) writes a persistent gda_capture_<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>_<seq>.png copy after the image is read and returns saved_path, so target='game' no longer silently ignores save; saving requires the write capability.

after_frames.description: target='game' only: wait this many rendered frames before capturing (integer >= 0, default: 0 = capture immediately); combined with when, the frame budget must be spent first. target='editor' rejects it because the editor capture runs synchronously on the main thread and cannot yield frames. Game-target results report when_satisfied_frame and captured_frame (captured_frame > when_satisfied_frame)

annotate.description: Applies to both targets: when true the output image is annotated with numbered red boxes around UI controls and the result gains an elements array of {id, path, type, text, position, size} in final-image pixels whose ids match the box numbers (text is omitted when empty, elements_truncated marks a 200-element cap); the editor target marks editor UI controls (window-level controls with space='window'), while target='game' marks Controls of the running game, annotated inside the game process (default: false)

annotate_nodes.description: Applies to both targets: array of 1-50 scene node path strings to mark with numbered blue boxes (ids count independently from the red UI-control annotate boxes, starting at 1); the editor target resolves edited-scene paths while target='game' forwards the list for the game process to resolve absolute game paths; the result gains a node_elements array of {id, path, type, ok, position, size, visible, behind?, error?} in final-image pixels (one entry per input path, per-item failures carry ok:false plus error instead of failing the call; behind marks 3D nodes behind the camera; visible:false marks skipped boxes) plus node_truncated when the shared 200-box drawing budget with annotate is exceeded; single-item errors: node not found, unsupported node type, viewport incompatible (default: absent = disabled)

annotate_nodes_max.description: Optional self-imposed tighter cap (1-50, default: 50) on annotate_nodes length; the call fails when annotate_nodes holds more entries (default: absent = 50-entry server cap)

diff_against_last.description: Editor target only: when true the result gains a diff object comparing the final image with the previous editor capture (comparable, changed_ratio, changed_bbox, or a reason when not comparable); when the two sizes differ the shared top-left region is compared instead and the diff additionally reports size_mismatch=true plus current_size {x, y} alongside baseline_size (default: false)

diff_image.description: Editor target only: when true with diff_against_last, the result additionally gains diff_image_data (base64 PNG) highlighting changed_bbox on a copy of the final image; requires diff_against_last, default false = numbers only; not returned when the diff is not comparable or has no changed_bbox; counts toward the PNG/JSON response limits (default: false)

max_dimension.description: Applies to both targets: downscale the output image so its longest side is at most this many pixels (64-4096); never upscales (default: no scaling); with target='game' the downscale is applied inside the game process. Applied last: region crop first, then scale, then this cap — when both are given max_dimension wins and width/height report the final size

region.description: Applies to both targets: crop the captured image to {x, y, width, height} in pixels (width/height must be positive); the rect is clamped to the image and an empty intersection fails with region_out_of_bounds; with target='game' the crop is applied inside the game process; example: {x: 0, y: 0, width: 640, height: 480}

save.description: Applies to both targets: when true a persistent copy of the PNG is written after the image is produced (editor target: directly; game target: after the editor reads it back from the OS-cache transport file), the result gains saved_path (and path for compatibility) and the destination keeps the 20 most recent gda_capture files (default: false)

save_dir.description: Directory for the save copy, applies to both targets: a res:// directory inside the project root (created recursively) or an absolute path inside the GDA captures directory; any other user:// or outside-project path is rejected with path rejected. Passing save_dir implies save=true. Default: the GDA captures directory

scale.description: Applies to both targets: integer nearest-neighbour upscale factor (1-8, default: 1) applied after the region crop and before max_dimension. The editor target returns the image inline and only writes a file when save=true; game-target captures are always written to the OS cache as the transport mechanism

space.description: Editor target only: 'viewport' (default) captures the editor 2D viewport with a 3D fallback; 'window' captures the editor main window root viewport exactly as shown on screen, including docks, toolbars and the 2D grid/selection overlays

target.description: Target to capture: 'editor' (default) grabs the editor 2D viewport with a fallback to the 3D viewport; 'game' captures the running game's root window over the runtime channel — requires a game launched from the editor whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension

timeout_ms.description: Response timeout in milliseconds for target='game' (default: 5000, max: 25000); ignored for target='editor'; when after_frames/when delay a game capture it also bounds the in-game wait and the game answers with a structured error (code when_timeout, plus frames_waited) on expiry. The host waits timeout_ms + 2000 ms and that budget must stay below the 30 s HTTP transport timeout, so 25000 ms is the hard cap — split long waits into shorter calls

wait_ready.description: Only for target='game': wait for the game process to report ready (gda:ready) before failing; while the game is starting, the request is queued and replayed as soon as readiness arrives. Set false to fail immediately (previous behaviour). Default: true

when.description: target='game' only: GDScript expression evaluated once per rendered frame inside the game; the capture fires when it is true (empty string = no condition). It runs with the current scene as the base instance, so node lookups such as get_node("HUD/MessageLabel").text != "" work directly. The result reports when_satisfied_frame (frame where the condition first held) and captured_frame (next rendered frame, read for the image; captured_frame > when_satisfied_frame), so the image reflects the state after the condition became true. A malformed expression fails immediately with a structured error (code when_parse_error) carrying the Expression error text; a condition that never becomes true returns a structured error (code when_timeout) bounded by timeout_ms. target='editor' rejects it

tools.name: capture_game_viewport
tools.description: Capture the running game's viewport as a PNG image over the runtime debug channel, returned as a base64-encoded string. Requires a game launched from the editor whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension. Optional timeout_ms bounds the capture wait (default 5000, max 25000; the host waits timeout_ms + 2000 ms, below the 30 s transport timeout); when after_frames/when delay the capture it also bounds the in-game wait and the game answers with a structured error (code when_timeout, plus frames_waited) on expiry. Optional after_frames (integer >= 0) waits that many rendered frames and optional when (a GDScript expression re-evaluated every rendered frame with the current scene as base instance) holds the capture until it is true - together they capture short-lived feedback such as a 2 s banner or a 0.7 s death screen without slowing the game down: act first, then capture with a condition. The condition is evaluated once per rendered frame; the frame where it first holds is reported as when_satisfied_frame, and the image is read on the next rendered frame and reported as captured_frame (captured_frame > when_satisfied_frame) so the picture shows the state after the condition became true. A malformed expression fails immediately with a structured error (code when_parse_error) carrying the Expression error text; evaluation errors keep the last message in the timeout error. Optional region {x, y, width, height} crops the captured image (clamped to the image; an empty intersection fails with region_out_of_bounds) and optional max_dimension (64-4096) downscales the output so its longest side is at most that many pixels; it never upscales. Optional scale (integer 1-8, default 1) nearest-neighbour upscales the output after the crop and before max_dimension, so max_dimension still caps the longest side when both are given and width/height report the final size. The game always writes the PNG to the OS cache as the transport mechanism before the editor reads it back and returns it inline. With annotate=true a numbered box is drawn for every Control element found in the game scene tree and the game-side result adds annotated=true plus an elements array {id,path,type,text,position,size} in image pixels, so UI elements can be located visually and then clicked with click_game_ui_element using the same row's path or text/text_index. id is a per-capture sequence number (1-based, unstable across captures) and cannot be passed to click_game_ui_element. Optional annotate_nodes (array of 1-50 game node paths) draws numbered blue boxes for scene nodes with per-item ok/error in node_elements plus node_truncated on budget truncation. Optional save (boolean, default false) and save_dir (res:// project directory or the GDA captures directory; default the GDA captures directory) write a persistent copy of the captured PNG after the editor reads it back, return saved_path, and require the write capability even though the capture tool itself is read-tier; without save/save_dir only the game-side OS-cache transport PNG exists.

after_frames.description: Wait this many rendered frames before capturing (integer >= 0, default: 0 = capture immediately); combined with when, the frame budget must be spent first and the capture fires on the first frame where both hold. Use it for short-lived events (a 2 s banner, a 0.7 s death screen) without slowing the game down: act first, then capture. timeout_ms bounds the wait and a never-met condition returns a structured error (code when_timeout) instead of hanging. The response reports when_satisfied_frame (the rendered frame where the condition first held) and captured_frame (the rendered frame read for the image); captured_frame is greater than when_satisfied_frame, so the image shows the state after the condition became true

annotate.description: Draw a numbered box for every Control element on the captured image (default: false); the game-side result also carries annotated=true plus an elements array {id,path,type,text,position,size} in image pixels; id is a per-capture sequence number — click with the same row's path or text/text_index, never with id

annotate_nodes.description: Draw numbered blue boxes for the listed game scene nodes (1-50 absolute paths, exact match first then '/'+path suffix match); per-item failures carry ok:false plus error and candidates without failing the call; result adds node_elements[{id,path,type,ok,position,size,visible,behind,error}] in final-image pixels plus node_truncated when the 200-box budget truncates node marks

annotate_nodes_max.description: Optional self limit 1-50 for annotate_nodes; the call fails when annotate_nodes is longer than this value

max_dimension.description: Downscale the output image so its longest side is at most this many pixels (64-4096); never upscales (default: no scaling). Applied last: region crop first, then scale, then this cap — when both are given max_dimension wins and width/height report the final size

region.description: Crop the captured image to {x, y, width, height} in viewport pixels (width/height must be positive); the rect is clamped to the image and an empty intersection fails with region_out_of_bounds

save.description: Write a persistent copy of the captured PNG after the editor reads it back from the game (default: false); the copy is named gda_capture_<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>_<seq>.png and its path is returned as saved_path. Saving requires the write capability even though the capture itself is read-tier; without save/save_dir the game only writes its OS-cache transport PNG

save_dir.description: Directory for the save copy: a res:// directory inside the project root (created recursively) or an absolute path inside the GDA captures directory; any other user:// or outside-project path is rejected with path rejected. Passing save_dir implies save=true. Default (save=true without save_dir): the GDA captures directory

scale.description: Integer nearest-neighbour upscale factor (1-8, default: 1) applied after the region crop and before max_dimension; useful for reading small HUD text from a cropped area. The game always writes the PNG to the OS cache directory as the transport mechanism before it is read back and returned inline; the editor target instead returns the image directly and only writes a file when save=true

timeout_ms.description: Response timeout in milliseconds (default: 5000, max: 25000); the capture is returned as a base64-encoded PNG; when after_frames/when delay the capture it also bounds the in-game wait and the game answers with a structured error (code when_timeout, plus frames_waited) on expiry. The host waits timeout_ms + 2000 ms and that budget must stay below the 30 s HTTP transport timeout, so 25000 ms is the hard cap — split long work into shorter calls

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready (gda:ready) before failing; while the game is starting, the request is queued and replayed as soon as readiness arrives. Set false to fail immediately (previous behaviour). Default: true

when.description: GDScript expression evaluated once per rendered frame inside the game process; the capture fires when it is true (empty string = no condition). It runs with the current scene as the base instance (falling back to the tree root when no scene is set), so node lookups such as get_node("HUD/MessageLabel").text != "" work directly. A malformed expression fails immediately with a structured error (code when_parse_error) carrying the Expression error text; evaluation errors keep the last message in the timeout error instead of failing the call. The response reports when_satisfied_frame/captured_frame with captured_frame greater than when_satisfied_frame, so the captured image is the rendered frame after the condition became true (not the same frame that evaluated it)

tools.name: click_editor_element
tools.description: Click an editor UI element resolved by its path, injecting warp, motion, press and release in one call; double_click adds a second press/release pair carrying the double-click flag. Element paths come from get_editor_ui_elements or hit_test_editor_point, so prefer this over raw-coordinate clicks. Optional 'button' accepts left, right or middle (default left) and 'warp' (default true) moves the physical cursor onto the element first; disable it for controls that react to hover. Optional 'observe' (default false) appends a fresh editor viewport capture to the result. Returns result with ok, path, type, button, double_click, window_id and position. Editor process only.

button.description: Mouse button to click: left, right or middle (default: left)

double_click.description: Send a second press/release pair carrying the double-click flag (default: false)

observe.description: Append a fresh editor viewport capture to the result (default: false)

path.description: Element path as returned by get_editor_ui_elements or hit_test_editor_point

warp.description: Warp the physical cursor onto the element center before clicking (default: true)

tools.name: click_game_ui_element
tools.description: Click a UI element in the running game process by node path or visible text over the runtime debug channel: the game enumerates its Control tree, resolves path (exact match first, otherwise a node path ending with '/'+path) or text (exact match over visible elements first, then substring) and injects a same-coordinate mouse_motion (mode 'event') first to refresh the game's hover state, then a mouse_button press/release pair at the element's global_rect centre through the same path as queue_game_input. Requires a game launched from the editor whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension and the game_runtime authorization gate. path (from get_game_ui_elements) or text (visible control text) selects the element — pass exactly one of them, path wins when both are given; text matches visible elements exactly first, then by substring, and text_index (default 0) picks the nth match when several match. The annotate id from capture_game_viewport is a per-capture sequence number and is not clickable — use the same row's path or its text instead; button_index (1=left default, 2=right, 3=middle) and double_click (default false, adds a second press/release pair) are optional. After injecting, the game compares the viewport hovered control with the resolved element: hit_path is the hovered control's node path (empty when nothing is hovered) and hit_mismatch is true when the hovered control is neither the resolved element nor one of its descendants — i.e. the click landed on a different control, typically one covering the target. A mismatch is not an error by default: the call succeeds, the result carries hit_path and hit_mismatch, and warning explains the mismatch. strict_hit (default false) instead fails the call with structured_error.code click_occluded (carrying target_path, hit_path and target_mouse_filter). max_elements caps the enumeration (default 1000, max 1000); timeout_ms defaults to 5000 (max 25000; the host waits timeout_ms + 2000 ms, below the 30 s transport timeout). One call performs both steps (enumerate + inject) and resolves with {"result":{"ok":true,"path":...,"position":{x,y},"viewport_position":{x,y},"window_position":{x,y},"clicks":n,"hit_path":...,"hit_mismatch":...}} plus warning when hit_mismatch is true; when the path is not found the error lists the element count and candidate paths.

double_click.description: Inject a second press/release pair (default: false)

max_elements.description: Maximum number of Control elements enumerated while resolving path (default: 1000, max: 1000)

path.description: Node path of the UI element to click, as returned by get_game_ui_elements (e.g. '/root/Main/Menu/StartButton'); an exact match wins, otherwise a path ending with '/'+path is used. Alternatively pass text/text_index instead — path wins when both are given; the annotate id from capture_game_viewport is a per-capture sequence number and is not clickable

strict_hit.description: Turn a hit mismatch into an error (default: false). The game reports hit_mismatch when the hovered control is neither the resolved element nor one of its descendants; strict_hit=false still succeeds and only reports hit_mismatch plus warning, strict_hit=true fails the call with code click_occluded

text.description: Visible text of the UI element to click (exact match over visible elements first, then substring); alternative to path — path wins when both are given

text_index.description: Selects the nth visible text match (0-based, default: 0); without it an ambiguous text fails listing candidates

timeout_ms.description: Response timeout in milliseconds (default: 5000, max: 25000); the game performs both the enumeration and the injection before answering. The host waits timeout_ms + 2000 ms and that budget must stay below the 30 s HTTP transport timeout, so 25000 ms is the hard cap — split long work into shorter calls

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready (gda:ready) before failing; while the game is starting, the request is queued and replayed as soon as readiness arrives. Set false to fail immediately (previous behaviour). Default: true

tools.name: click_input_mouse
tools.description: Click a point in the editor process by injecting a complete mouse sequence in one call: optional warp, a motion event, a press and a release, plus a second press/release pair when 'double_click' is true. 'position' is an object with numeric x and y fields, in pixels relative to the client area of the focused window — the editor main window while it has focus — so (0, 0) is that window's top-left corner, not a desktop/screen position and not the edited viewport. Prefer this composite over hand-chaining move_input_mouse, press_input_mouse_button and release_input_mouse_button; for editor UI elements prefer click_editor_element, which resolves the element to coordinates itself. 'button' accepts left, right or middle and defaults to left; 'warp' (default true) moves the physical cursor onto the target first. Controls that react to hover and drags depend on the physical mouse, so the effect may only settle on the next frame — re-observe before concluding that the click did nothing. Optional 'observe' (default false) appends a fresh editor viewport capture to the result. A running game is a separate process and will not receive these events. Returns result with ok true.

button.description: Mouse button to click: left, right or middle (default: left)

double_click.description: Send a second press/release pair to form a double click (default: false)

observe.description: Append a fresh editor viewport capture to the result (default: false)

position.description: Click position, object with numeric x and y fields, in pixels relative to the client area of the focused window

warp.description: Warp the physical cursor onto the position before clicking (default: true)

tools.name: close_editor_scene
tools.description: Close the currently edited scene tab and return the editor to an empty state when it was the last tab. Use it before opening or creating another scene, or when a scene is no longer needed. Only the current tab is closed: with multiple scene tabs open, call it repeatedly until no scene is open. Refuses to close when the scene has unsaved changes, so call save_editor_scene first. Returns result 'closed'.

tools.name: collect_game_evidence
tools.description: Collect a read-only evidence bundle from the running game process over the runtime debug channel in one round trip, without any automatic verdict: game status (same fields as get_game_status, with healthy/last_activity measured at request time), game screenshot (same semantics as capture_game_viewport immediate capture) and recent game errors (same list as get_debugger_errors). Requires a game launched from the editor whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension. Each section fails in isolation with an error object instead of failing the call; pass include_status/include_capture/include_errors=false to skip a section. Optional limit (integer 1-200, default 20) caps the errors section; region/max_dimension/scale mirror the capture parameters. Prefer this over three separate calls when the three observations must belong to the same moment; for a verdict, compare the sections yourself.

include_capture.description: Include the game screenshot section, same semantics as capture_game_viewport immediate capture (default: true)

include_errors.description: Include the recent game errors section, same list as get_debugger_errors (default: true)

include_status.description: Include the game status section, same fields as get_game_status (default: true)

limit.description: Maximum number of errors in the errors section, an integer from 1 to 200 (default: 20)

max_dimension.description: Downscale the capture so its longest side is at most this many pixels (64-4096); never upscales

region.description: Crop the captured image to {x, y, width, height} in viewport pixels; the rect is clamped to the image

scale.description: Integer nearest-neighbour upscale factor for the capture (1-8, default: 1), applied before max_dimension

timeout_ms.description: Response timeout in milliseconds (default: 5000, max: 25000). The host waits timeout_ms + 2000 ms and that budget must stay below the 30 s HTTP transport timeout, so 25000 ms is the hard cap

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready (gda:ready) before failing; while the game is starting, the request is queued and replayed as soon as readiness arrives. Set false to fail immediately (previous behaviour). Default: true

tools.name: commit_editor_undo_redo
tools.description: Commit the currently open undo/redo action so it appears in the editor's undo history as a single step. Use it to finalize a sequence started with create_editor_undo_redo_action and filled with add_editor_undo_redo_do or add_editor_undo_redo_undo calls; after committing, the action can no longer be extended. Returns result 'ok'.

tools.name: connect_animation_states
tools.description: Connect two existing states of the state machine rooted in the AnimationTree at 'animation_tree_path' (required string). Required 'from_state' and 'to_state'; optional 'condition' (string naming a bool parameter, e.g. "is_running") switches the transition to advance_mode AUTO with that advance_condition. Duplicate transitions are rejected. Use create_scene_animation_tree + add_animation_machine_state first.

animation_tree_path.description: Path of the AnimationTree owning both states

condition.description: Bool parameter name gating the transition, e.g. 'is_running'; sets advance_mode AUTO with that advance_condition

from_state.description: Source state name of the transition

to_state.description: Target state name of the transition

tools.name: control_game_tween
tools.description: Play, pause, stop or kill a game-side tween previously created with create_game_tween over the runtime debug channel; requires a game launched from the editor whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension. tween_id is the integer handle from creation and action is one of play, pause, stop or kill.

action.description: Control action: play, pause, stop or kill

timeout_ms.description: Response timeout in milliseconds (default: 5000, max: 25000). The host waits timeout_ms + 2000 ms and that budget must stay below the 30 s HTTP transport timeout, so 25000 ms is the hard cap

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready (gda:ready) before failing; while the game is starting, the request is queued and replayed as soon as readiness arrives. Set false to fail immediately (previous behaviour). Default: true

tools.name: copy_file
tools.description: Copy a single file to dest_path as plain byte-for-byte filesystem I/O with no editor resource tracking. Both 'path' and 'dest_path' are required res:// or user:// paths (absolute paths inside the project root are normalized to res://). Missing parent directories of dest_path are created recursively and an existing file at dest_path is overwritten. The .import and .uid sidecars are not copied or handled. Returns result (copied), from, to and overwritten. Use copy_resource_file when engine resource semantics are needed.

dest_path.description: Destination file path to write (res:// or user://); missing parent directories are created recursively and an existing file is overwritten

path.description: Source file path to copy (res:// or user://; must exist as a file)

tools.name: copy_resource_file
tools.description: Copy a file to dest_path inside res://. Both path (an existing res:// file) and dest_path are required; missing parent directories of dest_path are created recursively and an existing dest_path is overwritten. The copy is byte-for-byte: .import and .uid sidecars are not copied, imported assets need a reimport and a duplicated uid in the copied text resource may be reassigned by the editor scan. The editor file system is notified for dest_path and a scan runs afterwards. Returns result (copied), from and to. Use rename_resource_file/move_resource_file when you want to keep the file or remap references.

dest_path.description: Destination file path to write, e.g. res://assets/icon_copy.png; missing parent directories are created recursively and an existing file is overwritten

path.description: Source file path to copy, e.g. res://assets/icon.png; must exist

tools.name: create_animation
tools.description: Create a new Animation resource inside the default ('') library of the AnimationPlayer at 'player_path' (required string). Required 'name' (string, e.g. "walk"); optional 'length_sec' (number, seconds, default 1.0) and 'loop_mode' (int: 0 none, 1 linear loop, 2 pingpong; default 0). Fails if the name already exists — check get_animation_list first. Returns created metadata.

length_sec.description: Animation length in seconds (number, default: 1.0; must be > 0)

loop_mode.description: Loop mode: 0 none, 1 linear loop, 2 pingpong (integer, default: 0)

name.description: Animation name to create inside the default ('') library, e.g. 'walk'; must not already exist

player_path.description: Path of the AnimationPlayer node in the edited scene (e.g. 'AnimationPlayer')

tools.name: create_animation_track
tools.description: Add one track to animation 'anim_name' on player 'player_path' (both required strings). Required 'track_type': "value" or "method". Required 'node_path' (scene-relative target node); for value tracks also pass 'property' (string like "position:x" or "modulate:a") — the track path becomes <node_path>:<property> and the update mode is continuous; method tracks ignore 'property'. Duplicate track for the same path+type is rejected. Returns the new 'track_index' to use with insert_animation_keyframe.

anim_name.description: Animation name to add the track to; must already exist

node_path.description: Scene-relative path of the target node the track drives, e.g. 'Sprite2D'

player_path.description: Path of the AnimationPlayer node in the edited scene

property.description: Property to animate for value tracks, e.g. 'position:x' or 'modulate:a'; required when track_type is 'value', ignored for method tracks — the track path becomes <node_path>:<property>

track_type.description: Track kind: 'value' (animates a property) or 'method' (invokes a method per key)

tools.name: create_array_mesh
tools.description: Create an ArrayMesh with one triangle surface in memory and register it as memory://<name>; nothing is written to disk. Requires vertices (array of 1-65536 {x, y, z} objects; without indices every 3 vertices form one triangle). Optional normals (per-vertex {x, y, z}, must match vertices in length) and indices (integers in [0, vertex_count)). Returns class, name, path, object_id, object_id_str, mesh_ref, vertex_count, index_count, has_normals and surface_count; omitting normals yields a warning that shaded materials may render flat. Pass mesh_ref to set_mesh_surface_material or assign_mesh_to_instance.

indices.description: Optional triangle indices as integers in [0, vertex_count); each entry must reference a valid vertex

name.description: Registration name so later calls can reference the mesh as memory://name and via the returned object_id; when omitted only the object_id is registered

normals.description: Optional per-vertex normals as {x, y, z} objects; must match vertices in length when provided

vertices.description: Triangle vertex positions as 1-65536 {x, y, z} objects; without indices every 3 vertices form one triangle

tools.name: create_audiostream_wav
tools.description: Build an AudioStreamWAV from inline 'samples' and register it as 'memory://name' for later tools. 'format' accepts 8 or 16 (default 16) and any other value is rejected; 'mix_rate' defaults to 44100; 'stereo' false treats samples as mono while true expects flat interleaved L/R pairs; total frames (samples divided by channel count) must be between 1 and 1000000. Returns the WAV locator with format, mix_rate, stereo and frames in 'result'. Save it to disk before assigning it to a node property.

format.description: Sample format in bits; 8 or 16 (default 16); any other value is rejected

mix_rate.description: Mix rate in Hz stored on the WAV (default 44100); must be an integer in 1000..192000

name.description: Registration name for the new stream; the AudioStreamWAV stays alive as 'memory://name' for later tools

samples.description: Audio samples as floats in [-1, 1] (out-of-range values are clamped); mono samples when stereo is false, flat interleaved L/R pairs when stereo is true; total frames (samples divided by channel count) must be between 1 and 1000000

stereo.description: Treat samples as flat interleaved L/R pairs when true (default false treats them as mono)

tools.name: create_collision_shape
tools.description: Create a Shape2D or Shape3D resource in memory for a CollisionShape node. Required 'dim' is '2d' (Shape2D for CollisionShape2D) or '3d' (Shape3D for CollisionShape3D); required 'shape' is the type name: 2D 'circle', 'rectangle' or 'capsule', 3D 'sphere', 'box' or 'capsule', and must belong to dim. Required 'params' carries the dimensions: circle/sphere {radius}, rectangle {size {x, y} full extents}, box {size {x, y, z} full extents}, capsule {radius, height}, every number > 0. RectangleShape2D and BoxShape3D sizes are full extents and need no halving, unlike PhysicsServer2D rectangle shapes which take half extents; capsule radius/height map directly to CapsuleShape2D/CapsuleShape3D properties, unlike the server Array/Dictionary shape_set_data forms. The resource is pathless and registered for lookup via the returned object_id, so it can be passed to assign_collision_shape; memory:// resources from create_resource cannot be assigned to nodes. Returns class, object_id, object_id_str, path, dim and shape.

dim.description: Required. Physics dimension: '2d' creates a Shape2D resource for CollisionShape2D, '3d' creates a Shape3D resource for CollisionShape3D; the shape type must belong to it

params.description: Required. Shape dimensions object: circle/sphere {radius}, rectangle {size {x, y} full extents}, box {size {x, y, z} full extents}, capsule {radius, height}; every number must be > 0. RectangleShape2D and BoxShape3D sizes are full extents and need no halving, unlike PhysicsServer2D rectangle shapes which take half extents

shape.description: Required. Shape type name: 2D 'circle', 'rectangle' or 'capsule'; 3D 'sphere', 'box' or 'capsule'; must belong to dim

tools.name: create_csharp_script
tools.description: Create a new C# script file under res:// with pre-write validation. Requires path (must end in .cs) and source_code; overwrite defaults to false. Three gates fail with an actionable patch instead of a silent ok: the file stem must equal the declared class name, the class must be partial and derive from a ClassDB-known Godot base class, and the res:// root .csproj must reference the file (SDK-style globs count as referenced). Returns the CSharpFileRecord {path, class_name, csproj_ref_exists} plus base_class, project_file, is_dotnet_editor, verified/readback and a diagnostics object; the .cs diagnostics hint reports the .NET-editor state, the assembly build state and where in get_debugger_log to look. C# compiles out of band: run build_csharp_assembly afterwards and confirm via get_debugger_log, since nothing hot-reloads.

overwrite.description: Overwrite an existing file (default: false); false errors when the file already exists

path.description: C# file path to create under res:// (e.g. res://scripts/Player.cs); the file stem must equal the declared class name

source_code.description: C# source code; must declare one partial class deriving from a Godot base class, covered by the project .csproj

tools.name: create_curve_resource
tools.description: Create a Curve2D ('2d', default) or Curve3D ('3d') in memory and register it as memory://<name>; nothing is written to disk. Optional bake_interval (number greater than 0) sets the distance between baked points. Returns class, name, path, object_id, object_id_str and dimension; use set_curve_points to fill control points and get_curve_baked_points to read the baked polyline.

bake_interval.description: Distance between baked points in pixels; must be greater than 0 when provided

dimension.description: Curve dimension: '2d' creates a Curve2D (default), '3d' creates a Curve3D

name.description: Registration name so later calls can reference the curve as memory://name and via the returned object_id

tools.name: create_directory
tools.description: Create a directory inside the project, including any missing parent directories. path accepts a res:// absolute path (res://assets/audio) or a relative one (assets/audio); user:// is rejected. Idempotent: when the directory already exists the call succeeds and reports already_existed=true instead of failing. A newly created directory triggers an editor file system scan so subsequent resource operations see it immediately. Returns created (the normalized res:// path) and already_existed; errors when the directory cannot be created (invalid path or permission failure).

path.description: Directory to create below res:// (absolute like res://assets/audio or relative like assets/audio); missing parents are created recursively; idempotent when the directory already exists

tools.name: create_display_window
tools.description: Create a new sub-window in the editor process and show it on screen. Use it to display auxiliary content, e.g. a preview or dashboard. Returns result as the window_id, which the window tools (set_display_window_mode, set_display_window_size, delete_display_window and others) accept as their window_id argument. Optional mode (a Window.Mode enum value) and rect {x, y, w, h}; the rect defaults to 800x600 at the origin. Errors when the platform does not support subwindows.

mode.description: Window mode as a Window.Mode enum value, default 0 (windowed); note this enum differs from the DisplayServer.WindowMode used by set_display_window_mode

rect.description: Window rectangle as an object with integer x, y, w and h fields, e.g. {x: 100, y: 50, w: 800, h: 600}; defaults to 800x600 at the origin

tools.name: create_editor_scene
tools.description: Create a new empty scene with a root node of the given type in the editor. Use it to start building a new level; type defaults to Node, name defaults to NewRoot, and close_current (default false) closes the current scene tab automatically when it has no unsaved changes. Only the current tab is closed: with multiple scene tabs open, repeat close_editor_scene until no scene is open, otherwise this call fails fast with the neighboring tab reported in editor_state instead of waiting. Returns result with path, type and closed_previous; errors when the current scene is unsaved or type is not a Node subclass.

close_current.description: Close the current scene tab first if it has no unsaved changes (default: false; errors if the current scene is unsaved). Only the current tab is closed: with multiple scene tabs open, repeat close_editor_scene until no scene is open, otherwise create_editor_scene fails fast without entering the switch wait

name.description: Name of the new root node, defaults to 'NewRoot'

timeout_ms.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the editor to observe the new scene root after add_root_node (default: 2000, min: 50, max: 30000); on timeout the call errors with waited_ms, timeout_ms, node_released and editor_state diagnostics

type.description: Godot class name of the root node to create, e.g. 'Node2D' or 'Node3D'; must be a Node subclass, defaults to 'Node'

tools.name: create_editor_undo_redo_action
tools.description: Start a new undo/redo action in the editor's undo history with the given name. Use it to group several operations so a single undo step reverts them all. Must be followed by add_editor_undo_redo_do or add_editor_undo_redo_undo calls and finally commit_editor_undo_redo. Returns result 'ok'.

name.description: Human-readable name shown in the editor's undo history, e.g. 'Move player'; group related changes under one name so they revert together

tools.name: create_game_tween
tools.description: Create a property tween on a node in the running game process over the runtime debug channel; requires a game launched from the editor whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension. node_path selects the target node, property names the animated property (e.g. position, modulate:a) and target_value carries the final value converted with the same chain as execute_game_script set_property. duration (seconds, greater than 0) bounds one loop; optional trans (0-10, default 0 linear), ease (0-3, default 2 in_out), loops (integer >= 0, 0 means infinite, default 1) and speed_scale (greater than 0, default 1.0) shape the playback. Returns the game-side tween handle for control_game_tween.

duration.description: Tween duration in seconds for one loop (number greater than 0)

loops.description: Loop count, an integer >= 0 (0 means infinite loop; default 1)

node_path.description: Node path in the running game process, e.g. /root/Main/Player

property.description: Property to animate, e.g. position, scale or modulate:a; must exist on the node

target_value.description: Final value the property animates to, converted with the same chain as execute_game_script set_property (e.g. {"x": 10, "y": 20} for a Vector2, a plain number for scalar properties)

timeout_ms.description: Response timeout in milliseconds (default: 5000, max: 25000). The host waits timeout_ms + 2000 ms and that budget must stay below the 30 s HTTP transport timeout, so 25000 ms is the hard cap

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready (gda:ready) before failing; while the game is starting, the request is queued and replayed as soon as readiness arrives. Set false to fail immediately (previous behaviour). Default: true

tools.name: create_gridmap
tools.description: Create a GridMap node in the edited scene with the given cell size. Optional name (default GridMap), cell_size {x, y, z} in meters (default 1,1,1; every component must be > 0) and parent_path (omit to add at the scene root). Attach a MeshLibrary later with property_set, or build items with create_meshlibrary_item. Returns class, name, path and object_id.

cell_size.description: Cell size in meters as {x, y, z} (default: {"x":1,"y":1,"z":1}); every component must be > 0

name.description: GridMap node name (default: GridMap)

parent_path.description: Parent node path; omit to add at the scene root (errors when the scene has no root)

tools.name: create_meshlibrary_item
tools.description: Add an item with a mesh to a MeshLibrary created by create_resource (type MeshLibrary). Requires library (the memory:// reference name), item_id (>= 0, must be unused) and mesh (a Mesh resource reference: res:// or memory:// string or {"path": "res://..."} / {"resource": "memory://..."}); optional item_name display name. The item id is then usable as item in set_gridmap_cell and fill_gridmap_box. Returns result, item_id, item_name and mesh_class.

item_id.description: Item ID to assign (must be >= 0 and unused)

item_name.description: Display name stored on the item (default: empty)

library.description: MeshLibrary name from create_resource type MeshLibrary (memory:// reference)

mesh.description: Mesh resource reference: a res:// or memory:// string, or {"path": "res://..."} / {"resource": "memory://..."}; must resolve to a Mesh

tools.name: create_nav_2d_agent
tools.description: Create a 2D navigation agent on a map for avoidance-based movement. Requires 'map_rid' and 'position' ({x,y}); optional 'radius', 'max_speed' and 'avoidance_enabled' (default false). Returns the agent RID as 'rid'. Drive it each frame with set_nav_2d_agent_velocity; avoidance only steers while avoidance_enabled is true.

avoidance_enabled.description: Enable velocity avoidance for this agent (boolean, default: false)

map_rid.description: RID (integer) of the 2D navigation map, from create_nav_2d_map

max_speed.description: Maximum speed in meters per second used for avoidance (number)

position.description: Agent start position (object with x and y numbers)

tools.name: create_nav_2d_map
tools.description: Create a 2D navigation map on NavigationServer2D. Optional 'active' (default false) marks the map for pathfinding use. Returns the map RID as 'rid' — keep it and pass it to create_nav_2d_region and get_nav_2d_map_path. RIDs exist only in the running process; they are never persisted to scene files.

active.description: Mark the map active for pathfinding (boolean, default: false)

tools.name: create_nav_2d_region
tools.description: Create a 2D navigation region attached to a map created by create_nav_2d_map. Requires 'map_rid'; optional 'enabled' (default true) and 'navigation_layers' bitmask (default 1). Returns the region RID as 'rid'. Regions define the walkable area — a map with no region yields an empty path.

enabled.description: Whether the region participates in pathfinding (boolean, default: true)

map_rid.description: RID (integer) of the 2D navigation map, from create_nav_2d_map

navigation_layers.description: Navigation layers bitmask (integer, default: 1 — layer 1 only)

tools.name: create_nav_3d_agent
tools.description: Create a 3D navigation agent on a map for avoidance-based movement. Requires 'map_rid' and 'position' ({x,y,z}); optional 'radius', 'height', 'max_speed' and 'use_3d_avoidance' (default false). Returns the agent RID as 'rid'. Feed it a desired velocity each frame with set_nav_3d_agent_velocity. Read its state back with get_nav_3d_agent_state.

map_rid.description: RID (integer) of the 3D navigation map, from create_nav_3d_map
