max_speed.description: Maximum speed in meters per second used for avoidance (number)

position.description: Agent start position (object with x, y and z numbers)

use_3d_avoidance.description: Use 3D avoidance instead of 2D ground-plane avoidance (boolean, default: false)

tools.name: create_nav_3d_map
tools.description: Create a 3D navigation map on NavigationServer3D. Optional 'active' (default false), 'cell_size' (meters), 'cell_height' (meters) and 'up' ({x,y,z} direction, default Vector3.UP). Returns the map RID as 'rid' — pass it to create_nav_3d_region and get_nav_3d_map_path. RIDs exist only in the running process; they are never persisted to scene files.

active.description: Mark the map active for pathfinding (boolean, default: false)

cell_height.description: Map cell height in meters (number, default: 1.0)

cell_size.description: Map cell size in meters (number, default: 1.0)

up.description: Up direction (object with x, y and z numbers, default: {"x": 0, "y": 1, "z": 0})

tools.name: create_nav_3d_obstacle
tools.description: Create a 3D navigation obstacle on a map so avoidance agents steer around it. Requires 'map_rid' and 'position' ({x,y,z}); optional 'radius' and 'height' (meters). Returns the obstacle RID as 'rid'. Obstacles only affect agents with avoidance enabled; the RID stays valid until the process exits.

map_rid.description: RID (integer) of the 3D navigation map, from create_nav_3d_map

position.description: Obstacle position (object with x, y and z numbers)

tools.name: create_nav_3d_region
tools.description: Create a 3D navigation region attached to a map created by create_nav_3d_map. Requires 'map_rid'; optional 'enabled' (default true) and 'navigation_layers' bitmask (default 1). Returns the region RID as 'rid'. Assign a navigation mesh with set_nav_3d_region_navigation_mesh before querying paths. A disabled region is ignored by pathfinding.

enabled.description: Whether the region participates in pathfinding (boolean, default: true)

map_rid.description: RID (integer) of the 3D navigation map, from create_nav_3d_map

navigation_layers.description: Navigation layers bitmask (integer, default: 1 — layer 1 only)

tools.name: create_os_process
tools.description: Start an executable as a detached background process and return immediately. Use it for long-running or fire-and-forget programs; keep the returned PID to kill it later with kill_os_process. Unlike execute_os_process it does not wait for the process or capture output. Requires 'path' (string) and 'arguments' (array of strings); returns the process PID.

arguments.description: Command line arguments passed to the process; non-string entries are ignored

path.description: Executable to start (full path, or name resolved via PATH)

tools.name: create_path_node
tools.description: Create a Path2D/Path3D node in the edited scene bound to a curve created by create_curve_resource. Requires 'name' and 'curve' (the memory:// reference); the curve type decides the node type (Curve2D creates Path2D, Curve3D creates Path3D). Optional 'parent_path' (default: scene root; omit only while the scene has no root, in which case the new node becomes the root). Sets scene ownership so the node is saved. Returns the new node 'path', 'type', 'curve' and an 'undo' hint describing how to remove the node via delete_scene_node.

curve.description: Registration name of a curve from create_curve_resource (memory://name); a Curve2D creates a Path2D, a Curve3D creates a Path3D

name.description: Path node name (e.g. 'EnemyPath')

parent_path.description: Parent node path in the edited scene; omit only while the scene has no root, in which case the new path node becomes the root

tools.name: create_physics_2d_area
tools.description: Create a 2D physics area and return its RID handle. Areas detect overlaps and can apply effects such as gravity over their volume, unlike bodies which collide; use set_physics_2d_area_monitorable to control whether other areas can monitor it. Returns an object with the numeric RID id and an is_valid flag

tools.name: create_physics_2d_body
tools.description: Create a 2D physics body in the physics server and return its RID handle. Pass the returned RID to set_physics_2d_body_mode, apply_physics_2d_body_force, apply_physics_2d_body_impulse, set_physics_2d_body_state and get_physics_2d_body_state. The body is a server-side object with no scene node, so it is driven only through these tools and nothing appears in the editor scene tree. Returns an object with the numeric RID id and an is_valid flag

tools.name: create_physics_2d_circle_shape
tools.description: Create a 2D circle shape in PhysicsServer2D and return its RID handle. The RID cannot be assigned directly to CollisionShape2D.shape, which expects a Shape2D resource; to bridge it to a node, create a .tres via save_resource(class_type='CircleShape2D') and set CollisionShape2D.shape with set_property using type_hint='Resource'. The RID is only usable with physics server queries such as set_physics_2d_shape_data and intersect_physics_2d_shape

tools.name: create_physics_2d_joint
tools.description: Create a 2D physics joint linking two bodies and return its RID handle. Requires type: pin, groove or damped_spring; pin needs anchor and optionally body_a/body_b, groove needs groove1_a, groove2_a and anchor_b, damped_spring needs anchor_a, anchor_b and body_a. Bodies are the RIDs from create_physics_2d_body. Returns the joint RID, or an error when required per-type parameters are missing

anchor.description: Optional. Pin joint anchor as a Vector2 object with x and y fields (used for type='pin')

anchor_a.description: Optional. Damped spring anchor on body A as a Vector2 object (used for type='damped_spring')

anchor_b.description: Optional. Groove joint anchor on body B as a Vector2 object (used for type='groove')

body_a.description: Optional. RID id of the first body, e.g. from create_physics_2d_body

body_b.description: Optional. RID id of the second body; the joint connects body A to the world when omitted

groove1_a.description: Optional. First groove point as a Vector2 object (used for type='groove')

groove2_a.description: Optional. Second groove point as a Vector2 object (used for type='groove')

type.description: Required. Joint kind: 'pin', 'groove' or 'damped_spring'; each kind needs its own parameter set (see below)

tools.name: create_physics_3d_area
tools.description: Create a 3D physics area and return its RID handle. Areas detect overlaps and can apply effects such as gravity and damping over their volume, unlike bodies which collide; use set_physics_3d_area_param, set_physics_3d_area_transform and set_physics_3d_area_space to configure it. Returns an object with the numeric RID id and an is_valid flag

tools.name: create_physics_3d_body
tools.description: Create a 3D physics body in the physics server and return its RID handle. Pass the returned RID to set_physics_3d_body_mode, set_physics_3d_body_transform, apply_physics_3d_body_force, apply_physics_3d_body_impulse, apply_physics_3d_body_torque and set_physics_3d_body_state. The body is a server-side object with no scene node, driven only through these tools. Returns an object with the numeric RID id and an is_valid flag

tools.name: create_physics_3d_joint
tools.description: Create a 3D physics joint linking two bodies and return its RID handle. Requires type: pin, hinge, slider, cone_twist or generic_6dof, and body_a_rid from create_physics_3d_body; body_b_rid and the joint-specific transforms are optional. Pin takes local_a/local_b, hinge takes hinge_a/hinge_b, and the remaining types take ref_a/ref_b. Returns the joint RID, or an error when required parameters are missing

body_a_rid.description: Required. RID id of the first body, e.g. from create_physics_3d_body

body_b_rid.description: Optional. RID id of the second body; the joint connects body A to the world when omitted

hinge_a.description: Optional. Hinge joint frame on body A as a Transform3D object (used for type='hinge')

hinge_b.description: Optional. Hinge joint frame on body B as a Transform3D object (used for type='hinge')

local_a.description: Optional. Pin joint local anchor on body A as a Vector3 object (used for type='pin')

local_b.description: Optional. Pin joint local anchor on body B as a Vector3 object (used for type='pin')

ref_a.description: Optional. Reference frame on body A as a Transform3D object (used for 'slider', 'cone_twist' and 'generic_6dof')

ref_b.description: Optional. Reference frame on body B as a Transform3D object (used for 'slider', 'cone_twist' and 'generic_6dof')

type.description: Required. Joint kind: 'pin', 'hinge', 'slider', 'cone_twist' or 'generic_6dof'; each kind uses its own transform parameters

tools.name: create_physics_3d_soft_body
tools.description: Create a 3D soft body and return its RID handle. Soft bodies deform under physics forces instead of moving rigidly; assign a mesh with set_physics_3d_soft_body_mesh to give it shape. Returns an object with the numeric RID id and an is_valid flag

tools.name: create_physics_3d_sphere_shape
tools.description: Create a sphere shape in the physics server and return its RID handle. The RID cannot be assigned directly to CollisionShape3D.shape, which expects a SphereShape3D resource; to bridge it to a node, create a .tres via save_resource(class_type='SphereShape3D') and assign it with set_property using type_hint='Resource'. The RID is only usable with physics server queries such as set_physics_3d_shape_data, add_physics_3d_body_shape and intersect_physics_3d_shape

tools.name: create_primitive_mesh
tools.description: Create a PrimitiveMesh in memory and register it as memory://<name>; nothing is written to disk. type selects the mesh (box, capsule, plane, quad, sphere, torus, tube, text map to BoxMesh, CapsuleMesh, PlaneMesh, QuadMesh, SphereMesh, TorusMesh, TubeTrailMesh, TextMesh). Optional params applies property overrides such as size or radius; unknown properties are rejected and nothing is registered. Returns class, name, path, object_id, object_id_str, type and mesh_ref; pass mesh_ref to set_mesh_surface_material or assign_mesh_to_instance.

name.description: Registration name so later calls can reference the mesh as memory://name and via the returned object_id; when omitted only the object_id is registered

params.description: Optional property overrides applied to the new primitive, e.g. size, radius, height; unknown property names are rejected and nothing is registered

type.description: Primitive kind: one of box, capsule, plane, quad, sphere, torus, tube, text; maps to BoxMesh, CapsuleMesh, PlaneMesh, QuadMesh, SphereMesh, TorusMesh, TubeTrailMesh, TextMesh

tools.name: create_render_camera
tools.description: Create a server-side 3D camera and return its RID as result.rid. Configure its projection with set_render_camera_perspective or set_render_camera_orthogonal and place it with set_render_camera_transform. Cameras work with a scenario RID from create_render_scenario to define the viewpoint of a custom render scene. Returns an error if the RenderingServer is unavailable.

tools.name: create_render_canvas_item
tools.description: Create a server-side 2D canvas item and return its RID as result.rid. Use this to build custom 2D drawing independent of scene nodes, then draw shapes with add_render_canvas_item_rect, add_render_canvas_item_circle, add_render_canvas_item_texture_rect or add_render_canvas_item_line and control visibility with set_render_canvas_item_visible. Returns an error if the RenderingServer is unavailable.

tools.name: create_render_decal
tools.description: Create a server-side decal and return its RID as result.rid. A decal projects a texture onto nearby surfaces, e.g. bullet holes or signs. Note that no tool instantiates the decal into a scenario, so its use is currently limited. Returns an error if the RenderingServer is unavailable.

tools.name: create_render_fog_volume
tools.description: Create a server-side volumetric fog volume and return its RID as result.rid. shape and size may be set at creation, or later with set_render_fog_volume_shape. Fog volumes add localized volumetric fog in 3D scenes when combined with an environment that has volumetric fog enabled. Returns an error if the RenderingServer is unavailable.

shape.description: Fog volume shape: 0=ellipsoid, 1=cone, 2=cylinder, 3=box, 4=world (default: 0); can be changed later with set_render_fog_volume_shape

size.description: Fog volume size {x, y, z}; example: {x: 4, y: 2, z: 4}

tools.name: create_render_light
tools.description: Create a server-side light and return its RID as result.rid. type selects directional, omni or spot and defaults to directional. Pair with set_render_light_param and set_render_light_color. Use it to light custom 3D scenes assembled from server-side RIDs. Returns an error on unknown light types or if the RenderingServer is unavailable.

type.description: Light type: directional (sun-like, parallel rays), omni (point light), or spot (cone light); default: directional

tools.name: create_render_material
tools.description: Create a server-side material and return its RID as result.rid. Materials feed shader parameters into surfaces; set them with set_render_material_param and assign via set_render_mesh_surface_material. Note that no tool attaches a shader to a material, so the material only takes effect with external shader setup (e.g. code_execute). Returns an error if the RenderingServer is unavailable.

tools.name: create_render_mesh
tools.description: Create a server-side mesh to hold geometry, returning its RID as result.rid. A mesh owns one or more surfaces built with add_render_mesh_surface; assign per-surface materials with set_render_mesh_surface_material. A mesh alone is not visible; it needs to be instanced into a scenario. Returns an error if the RenderingServer is unavailable.

tools.name: create_render_particles
tools.description: Create a server-side particle system and return its RID as result.rid. mode selects 2D (0) or 3D (1) and defaults to 3D. Pair with set_render_particles_emitting, set_render_particles_lifetime and restart_render_particles. Note that no tool instantiates the system into a scenario, so visible emission requires external setup (e.g. code_execute). Returns an error if the RenderingServer is unavailable.

tools.name: create_render_reflection_probe
tools.description: Create a server-side reflection probe and return its RID as result.rid. A reflection probe captures surrounding geometry and lights to feed reflective materials. Use it to add local reflections to custom 3D scenes, though no tool instantiates the probe into a scenario. Returns an error if the RenderingServer is unavailable.

tools.name: create_render_scenario
tools.description: Create a server-side 3D scenario and return its RID as result.rid. A scenario hosts 3D cameras, lights, meshes and fog; use it to assemble a custom render scene outside the node tree. Pass the RID to set_render_scenario_environment to attach an environment. Returns an error if the RenderingServer is unavailable.

tools.name: create_render_shader
tools.description: Create a server-side shader and return its RID as result.rid. Optional code sets the shader source immediately; set_render_shader_code replaces it later. Note that no tool can attach a shader to a material, so the shader RID is mainly useful for testing. Returns an error if the RenderingServer is unavailable.

code.description: Shader source code (optional); can be replaced later with set_render_shader_code

tools.name: create_render_sky
tools.description: Create a server-side sky and return its RID as result.rid. Assign a material with set_render_sky_material. Note that no tool can attach a sky to an environment, so the sky RID is mainly useful for testing. Returns an error if the RenderingServer is unavailable.

tools.name: create_render_texture_from_image
tools.description: Create a server-side 2D texture from an image file and return its RID as result.rid. image_path accepts res://, user:// or absolute paths; relative paths are not supported. Pass the RID to add_render_canvas_item_texture_rect. Returns an error if the image fails to load.

image_path.description: Image file path; accepts res://, user:// or absolute paths (relative paths are not supported); example: 'res://icon.svg'

tools.name: create_render_viewport
tools.description: Create a server-side viewport and return its RID as result.rid. Configure it with set_render_viewport_size and set_render_viewport_clear_mode. Note that no tool can attach a camera or canvas to a viewport, so standalone viewports cannot be rendered; the RID is useful mainly for external composition. Returns an error if the RenderingServer is unavailable.

tools.name: create_resource
tools.description: Instantiate a Resource subclass by class name (type) in memory. type accepts both engine classes from ClassDB and global script classes (GDScript class_name / C# [GlobalClass]); abstract or invalid scripts are rejected, and C# classes are gated by is_abstract plus a real new() probe because can_instantiate may misreport them. Pass name to register the instance so later calls can reference it as memory://name. Returns the reference with object_id and object_id_str, which serve as locators for set_resource_property, get_resource_property and save_resource. When the global class cache misses, .cs/.gd sources under res:// are scanned for a matching [GlobalClass]/class_name declaration (stopping after 500 files with guidance to open the editor) before reporting an unknown class. Errors when type is not a known class or not an instantiable Resource subclass.

name.description: Registration name so later calls can reference the instance as memory://name and via the returned object_id; optional but recommended

type.description: Resource class to instantiate, e.g. Resource, Curve2D, PackedScene; accepts both engine classes from ClassDB and global script classes (GDScript class_name / C# [GlobalClass]); abstract or invalid scripts are rejected; C# classes are gated by is_abstract plus a real new() probe because can_instantiate may misreport them

tools.name: create_scene_animation_player
tools.description: Create an AnimationPlayer node in the edited scene under 'parent_path' (required string, scene-relative node path, e.g. "Root/Actors"). Optional 'name' (string, default AnimationPlayer). Returns the new node 'path' plus an 'undo' hint; follow up with create_animation to add clips.

name.description: Node name for the new AnimationPlayer (string, default: AnimationPlayer)

parent_path.description: Parent node path in the edited scene (e.g. 'Root' or 'Root/Actors')

tools.name: create_scene_animation_tree
tools.description: Create an AnimationTree under required 'parent_path' in the edited scene, with an empty AnimationNodeStateMachine as its tree_root. Optional 'name' (string, default AnimationTree) and optional 'anim_player' (scene-relative AnimationPlayer path, e.g. "Root/AnimationPlayer") wired into the tree's animation_player property. Returns 'path', initial 'states' list and a 'next' hint pointing at add_animation_machine_state.

anim_player.description: Scene-relative AnimationPlayer path to wire into the tree's animation_player property, e.g. 'Root/AnimationPlayer'

name.description: Node name for the new AnimationTree (string, default: AnimationTree)

parent_path.description: Parent node path in the edited scene (e.g. 'Root')

tools.name: create_scene_node
tools.description: Create a new node in the currently edited scene. Provide 'type' (any Node subclass, default Node) and 'name' (default NewNode); omit 'parent_path' only while the scene has no root, otherwise pass the parent node path. Optional 'properties' object applies values right after creation through the same conversion chain as property_set (NodePath strings become node references, resource references are resolved, and an inline resource description such as {"type": "RectangleShape2D", "properties": {...}} creates a pathless sub-resource saved as a sub_resource) — any failing property frees the new node and reports the property name. Returns the new node 'path', the 'applied_properties' array (property names applied without error; a property may still have been adjusted by the engine — it then also appears in 'property_warnings'), the 'inline_resources' array ({property, type} entries present only when inline descriptions were applied) and an 'undo' hint describing how to remove the node via delete_scene_node. When the engine adjusts or flags a value after a successful set, the response additionally includes 'property_warnings', an array of {path, property, warning} objects; the field is absent when there are no warnings.

name.description: Node name (string, default: NewNode); optional — the node is named NewNode when the parameter is omitted

parent_path.description: Parent node path in the edited scene (e.g. 'Player' or 'Player/Weapon'); omit only while the scene has no root — required once the scene already has a root. The response includes scene_path and scene_unsaved so the caller can confirm which scene received the node

properties.description: Optional map of property names to values applied right after creation via the same conversion chain as property_set (object, e.g. {"visible": false, "position": {"x": 10, "y": 20}}); any failing property frees the new node and reports the failing name

type.description: Node class type (string, default: Node); optional — a Node is created when the parameter is omitted. Must be a Node subclass, e.g. Node2D, Sprite2D — other classes error

tools.name: create_scene_tree_timer
tools.description: Act on the running game process's SceneTree over the runtime channel — requires a game launched from the editor whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension, and game_runtime authorization. Unlike editor scene tools, this never touches the editor's own scene tree: without a running game it returns a structured error. Create a SceneTreeTimer in that game SceneTree, used with await or a timeout callback for delayed game logic. Requires 'delay_sec'; optional 'process_always' (default true — runs while the game tree is paused) and 'process_in_physics' (default false). Returns 'ok' with a note that the timer was created in the game process: the SceneTreeTimer object cannot be returned across processes, so observe its effect (an await or a timeout callback) in the game instead of holding a reference.

process_always.description: Process even while the scene tree is paused (boolean, default: true)

process_in_physics.description: Count down in the physics step instead of the process step (boolean, default: false)

tools.name: create_script
tools.description: Create a new GDScript file and save it to disk. Requires path and source_code; source_code is written as UTF-8, so non-ASCII (e.g. CJK) content round-trips byte-exact. The script is compiled before saving and compilation errors abort the call with parser output. overwrite defaults to false — an existing file errors unless overwrite=true. Returns path, class and overwritten; cache_refreshed reports whether the freshly written file was re-read into the resource cache (cache_refresh_error is included when that reload failed); global_class_name is included when the script declares one. The file content is read back from disk after saving and verified against source_code (see verified/readback/disk_bytes/content_hash fields — disk_bytes is the read-back byte length and content_hash is the FNV-1a-64 hex of the bytes actually read from disk, with content_hash_algo naming the algorithm, so a successful response is self-proving without a follow-up read); locked-file write failures surface as verified=false instead of silent success. Do not issue create_script calls for the same file in parallel requests — serial writes to the same path are not synchronized. After changing a script that the running game uses, call reload_game_scripts first and then reload_current_scene (or retry the operation) — reloading the scene alone does not guarantee the on-disk version is re-read (CACHE_MODE_REUSE).

overwrite.description: Overwrite an existing file (default: false); false errors when the file already exists

path.description: Script file path to create (e.g. res://scripts/enemy.gd)

source_code.description: GDScript source code; compiled before saving, compilation errors abort the call

tools.name: create_shaped_text
tools.description: Create a shaped text object in the TextServer and return its RID id as 'result'. Optional 'direction' (0=auto, 1=ltr, 2=rtl) and 'orientation' (0=horizontal, 1=vertical) select layout behavior, both default to auto/horizontal. Pass the id as shaped_rid to add_shaped_text_string to add text, then to get_shaped_text_size for the measured size. Errors if the TextServer is unavailable.

tools.name: create_spriteframes
tools.description: Create a SpriteFrames resource in memory and register it as memory://<name>; nothing is written to disk. As a side effect the built-in 'default' animation is removed, so add animations explicitly with add_spriteframes_animation before adding frames with add_spriteframes_frame. Returns class, name, path, object_id and default_animation_removed.

default_animation.description: Optional animation created immediately as an empty animation (engine-default fps/loop). Use 'default' to match the AnimatedSprite2D default animation property, so a node that never sets animation keeps a deterministic first animation in the editor instead of falling back to an arbitrary list entry; runtime playback still needs an explicit play() call or property_set on the node

name.description: Resource name used as the memory:// reference for later tools (e.g. 'hero_walk')

tools.name: create_text_font
tools.description: Create a font object in the TextServer and return its RID id as 'result'. Use it before the other text tools: the id is passed as font_rid to set_text_font_data, set_text_font_antialiasing, set_text_font_hinting and add_shaped_text_string. Every font tool requires a valid font_rid obtained here. Errors if the TextServer is unavailable.

tools.name: create_theme_resource
tools.description: Create an empty Theme resource on disk at path (a res:// .tres path — res:// only; user:// rejected). Missing directories are created and the editor file system is refreshed after saving; an existing file is never overwritten. Optional base_type (e.g. Control) is stored as resource metadata for reference — Godot themes carry no global base type, so actual items are added with set_theme_color, set_theme_constant, set_theme_font_size and set_theme_stylebox_flat. Returns ok with the saved path.

base_type.description: Base type stored as resource metadata for reference, e.g. 'Control'; Godot themes carry no global base type

path.description: Destination .tres path inside res:// (res:// only, user:// rejected), e.g. 'res://themes/main.tres'; missing directories are created and an existing file is never overwritten

tools.name: create_tilemap
tools.description: Create a TileMap node in the edited scene and attach a default TileSet with the given tile size. Optional name (default TileMap), tile_size in pixels (default 16), format (cell quadrant size, default 16) and parent_path (omit to add at the scene root). Returns class, name, path and object_id.

name.description: TileMap node name (default: TileMap)

parent_path.description: Parent node path; omit to add at the scene root (errors when the scene has no root)

tile_size.description: Tile size in pixels, sets the default TileSet tile_size (default: 16)

tools.name: create_tilemap_tileset
tools.description: Create a TileSet resource in memory and register it as memory://<name>; nothing is written to disk. Optional name (default TileSet) and tile_size in pixels (default 16). add_tilemap_atlas_source, add_tilemap_physics_layer and set_tilemap_tile_collision reference it by name. Returns class, name, path and object_id.

name.description: Resource name used as the memory:// reference for later tools (default: TileSet)

tools.name: csharp_call_method
tools.description: Call a C# method through the frozen GdaCSharpBridge ABI (call_method) with overload resolution by argument count. The locator takes exactly one of object_id, object_id_str, memory or path; args is a JSON array of at most 16 entries. With runtime=editor (default) the object is resolved in the editor process and invoked via the GdaCSharpBridge engine singleton (requires a .NET editor build with the bridge registered). With runtime=game the scene-path locator is forwarded to the game bridge over the runtime channel (requires a running .NET game with GdaCSharpRuntime; game-side args cross as JSON-native values only). Always needs the code_execute authorization gate, plus game_runtime when runtime=game. Returns the serialized return value.

args.description: Call arguments as a JSON array (max 16 entries); editor values deserialize with full Variant fidelity, game values cross as JSON-native values only

memory.description: Memory resource name registered via create_resource (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id, object_id_str and path

method.description: C# method name to call (params-array overloads are packed from trailing arguments by the bridge; overloads are matched by argument count with per-argument conversion)

object_id.description: Live object id from a previous result (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id_str, memory and path

object_id_str.description: Live object id as a decimal string for ids beyond 32-bit range (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id, memory and path

path.description: Scene node path in the edited scene (editor) or the running game (runtime=game), or a res:// resource path (editor only). memory:// is rejected here — pass the bare name in memory instead

runtime.description: Target process: editor (default, resolve the locator in the editor and call the GdaCSharpBridge engine singleton) or game (forward to the game bridge over the runtime channel; only the scene-path locator form is accepted, needs a running .NET game with GdaCSharpRuntime)

timeout_ms.description: Response timeout in milliseconds for runtime=game (default: 5000, max: 25000); rejected when runtime=editor

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready before failing when runtime=game (default: true); rejected when runtime=editor

tools.name: csharp_get_property
tools.description: Read a C# member through the frozen GdaCSharpBridge ABI (get_prop): engine properties plus C# properties and fields that GDScript cannot see, including non-public members when the bridge allows them. The locator takes exactly one of object_id, object_id_str, memory or path. With runtime=editor (default) the object is resolved in the editor process and read via the GdaCSharpBridge engine singleton (requires a .NET editor build with the bridge registered). With runtime=game the scene-path locator is forwarded to the game bridge over the runtime channel (requires a running .NET game with GdaCSharpRuntime; object_id, object_id_str and memory locators are rejected there). Always needs the code_execute authorization gate, plus game_runtime when runtime=game. Returns the serialized member value.

allow_non_public.description: Allow non-public C# members for this read (default false: only public engine properties, properties and fields resolve); when true the bridge also reads private and internal members, and the matching write path honors the same flag for writes

memory.description: Memory resource name registered via create_resource (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id, object_id_str and path

object_id.description: Live object id from a previous result (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id_str, memory and path

object_id_str.description: Live object id as a decimal string for ids beyond 32-bit range (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id, memory and path

path.description: Scene node path in the edited scene (editor) or the running game (runtime=game), or a res:// resource path (editor only). memory:// is rejected here — pass the bare name in memory instead

property.description: C# member name to read: engine property, C# property or field (indexers are rejected by the bridge)

runtime.description: Target process: editor (default, resolve the locator in the editor and call the GdaCSharpBridge engine singleton) or game (forward to the game bridge over the runtime channel; only the scene-path locator form is accepted, needs a running .NET game with GdaCSharpRuntime)

timeout_ms.description: Response timeout in milliseconds for runtime=game (default: 5000, max: 25000); rejected when runtime=editor

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready before failing when runtime=game (default: true); rejected when runtime=editor

tools.name: csharp_list_members
tools.description: List members visible to GDScript and C# callers through Object reflection (get_method_list/get_property_list/get_signal_list) for pre-call discovery before csharp_get_property/csharp_call_method/csharp_subscribe_event. The locator takes exactly one of object_id, object_id_str, memory or path. With runtime=editor (default) the object is resolved in the editor process and its method, property and signal tables are read directly with no bridge required. With runtime=game the scene-path locator is forwarded over the runtime channel and the three tables are read on the running game node (object_id, object_id_str and memory locators are rejected there; no bridge required). Optional kind (method|property|signal|all, default all) restricts which tables are searched, name_contains filters member names case-insensitively, and limit (1-1000, default 200) plus offset page the matched members across the three tables in methods then properties then signals order; filtering and paging for runtime=game run inside the running game so the big inherited tables never cross the runtime channel. Always needs the code_execute authorization gate, plus game_runtime when runtime=game. Returns result {methods, properties, signals, counts:{methods,properties,signals,returned,total}, truncated} where counts holds the matched totals per table plus how many members this page returned (returned) and matched in total (total), and truncated is true when more matched members remain after limit/offset; the default limit 200 is a behaviour change (D-07) that keeps responses inside client token limits, so call again with a larger limit or a later offset to collect the rest.

kind.description: Member table to return: method, property, signal or all (default: all); tables excluded by kind come back as empty arrays with a zero count so counts stays readable

limit.description: Maximum number of members returned across the three tables, in methods then properties then signals order (integer 1-1000, default: 200). Behaviour change (D-07): this call used to return every inherited member and could exceed client token limits; raise limit explicitly or page with offset when you need the full table

memory.description: Memory resource name registered via create_resource (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id, object_id_str and path

name_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on member names, e.g. 'visible' or 'Get' (default: no filter); an empty string is rejected. Narrowing the needle is the fastest way to reach one member in the inherited table

object_id.description: Live object id from a previous result (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id_str, memory and path

object_id_str.description: Live object id as a decimal string for ids beyond 32-bit range (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id, memory and path

offset.description: Number of matched members to skip before applying limit, counted in the same methods then properties then signals order (default: 0); an offset past the end returns empty arrays with counts.total telling you how many existed

path.description: Scene node path in the edited scene (editor) or the running game (runtime=game), or a res:// resource path (editor only). memory:// is rejected here — pass the bare name in memory instead

runtime.description: Target process: editor (default, resolve the locator in the editor and read Object reflection directly with no bridge required) or game (forward the scene-path locator over the runtime channel and read Object reflection on the running game node; only the scene-path locator form is accepted)

timeout_ms.description: Response timeout in milliseconds for runtime=game (default: 5000, max: 25000); rejected when runtime=editor

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready before failing when runtime=game (default: true); rejected when runtime=editor

tools.name: csharp_set_property
tools.description: Write a C# member through the frozen GdaCSharpBridge ABI (set_prop): engine properties plus C# properties and fields that GDScript cannot see, including non-public members when allow_non_public is true (read-only members and indexers are rejected). The locator takes exactly one of object_id, object_id_str, memory or path, and value carries the new member value. With runtime=editor (default) the object is resolved in the editor process and written via the GdaCSharpBridge engine singleton (requires a .NET editor build with the bridge registered). With runtime=game the scene-path locator is forwarded to the game bridge over the runtime channel (requires a running .NET game with GdaCSharpRuntime; object_id, object_id_str and memory locators are rejected there; game-side values cross as JSON-native values only). Always needs the code_execute authorization gate, plus game_runtime when runtime=game. Returns ok on success.

allow_non_public.description: Allow non-public C# members for this write (default false: only public engine properties, properties and fields resolve); when true the bridge also writes private and internal members, and the matching read path honors the same flag for reads

memory.description: Memory resource name registered via create_resource (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id, object_id_str and path

object_id.description: Live object id from a previous result (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id_str, memory and path

object_id_str.description: Live object id as a decimal string for ids beyond 32-bit range (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id, memory and path

path.description: Scene node path in the edited scene (editor) or the running game (runtime=game), or a res:// resource path (editor only). memory:// is rejected here — pass the bare name in memory instead

property.description: C# member name to write: engine property, C# property or field (indexers and read-only members are rejected by the bridge)

runtime.description: Target process: editor (default, resolve the locator in the editor and call the GdaCSharpBridge engine singleton) or game (forward to the game bridge over the runtime channel; only the scene-path locator form is accepted, needs a running .NET game with GdaCSharpRuntime)

timeout_ms.description: Response timeout in milliseconds for runtime=game (default: 5000, max: 25000); rejected when runtime=editor

value.description: New member value as JSON; editor values deserialize with full Variant fidelity, game values cross as JSON-native values only

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready before failing when runtime=game (default: true); rejected when runtime=editor

tools.name: csharp_subscribe_event
tools.description: Subscribe a receiver method to a C# event through the frozen GdaCSharpBridge ABI (subscribe): event arguments are forwarded to the receiver method call. The source locator takes exactly one of object_id, object_id_str, memory or path, and the receiver locator takes exactly one of target_object_id, target_object_id_str, target_memory or target_path. With runtime=editor (default) both objects are resolved in the editor process and linked via the GdaCSharpBridge engine singleton (requires a .NET editor build with the bridge registered). With runtime=game both scene-path locators are forwarded to the game bridge over the runtime channel (requires a running .NET game with GdaCSharpRuntime). Always needs the code_execute authorization gate, plus game_runtime when runtime=game. Returns the subscription token issued by the bridge.

event.description: C# event name on the source object (void-returning handlers with at most 4 parameters only)

memory.description: Memory resource name of the C# event source (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id, object_id_str and path

method.description: Receiver method name invoked with the forwarded event arguments

object_id.description: Live object id of the C# event source (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id_str, memory and path

object_id_str.description: Live object id of the C# event source as a decimal string (editor process only); mutually exclusive with object_id, memory and path

path.description: Scene node path of the C# event source in the edited scene (editor) or the running game (runtime=game), or a res:// resource path (editor only)

runtime.description: Target process: editor (default, resolve both locators in the editor and call the GdaCSharpBridge engine singleton) or game (forward to the game bridge over the runtime channel; only scene-path locator forms are accepted, needs a running .NET game with GdaCSharpRuntime)

target_memory.description: Memory resource name of the event receiver (editor process only); mutually exclusive with target_object_id, target_object_id_str and target_path

target_object_id.description: Live object id of the event receiver (editor process only); mutually exclusive with target_object_id_str, target_memory and target_path

target_object_id_str.description: Live object id of the event receiver as a decimal string (editor process only); mutually exclusive with target_object_id, target_memory and target_path

target_path.description: Scene node path of the event receiver in the edited scene (editor) or the running game (runtime=game), or a res:// resource path (editor only)

timeout_ms.description: Response timeout in milliseconds for runtime=game (default: 5000, max: 25000); rejected when runtime=editor

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready before failing when runtime=game (default: true); rejected when runtime=editor

tools.name: csharp_unsubscribe_event
tools.description: Release a C# event subscription created by csharp_subscribe_event through the frozen GdaCSharpBridge ABI (unsubscribe) so the receiver stops getting event arguments. The token comes from the result of csharp_subscribe_event and is scoped to one bridge instance: with runtime=editor (default) the subscription is released on the GdaCSharpBridge engine singleton (requires a .NET editor build with the bridge registered), with runtime=game it is forwarded to the game bridge over the runtime channel (requires a running .NET game with GdaCSharpRuntime; restarting the game already drops every subscription). Always needs the code_execute authorization gate, plus game_runtime when runtime=game. Returns ok on success; unknown or already-released tokens are rejected.

runtime.description: Target process: editor (default, release the subscription on the GdaCSharpBridge engine singleton) or game (forward to the game bridge over the runtime channel; needs a running .NET game with GdaCSharpRuntime)

timeout_ms.description: Response timeout in milliseconds for runtime=game (default: 5000, max: 25000); rejected when runtime=editor

token.description: Subscription token returned in the result of csharp_subscribe_event on the same bridge instance (editor singleton or the running game bridge); tokens are scoped to one bridge instance, restarting the game drops every subscription

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready before failing when runtime=game (default: true); rejected when runtime=editor

tools.name: delete_display_window
tools.description: Close and free a sub-window previously created with create_display_window. Use it to clean up windows that are no longer needed. Takes window_id as returned by create_display_window; errors when no window with the given id exists and refuses window_id 0, which is the editor main window and is never destroyed by this tool. The window is freed at the end of the frame. This tool is classified as a destructive side effect because it destroys an existing window.

window_id.description: window_id as returned by create_display_window; errors when no window with this id exists, and window_id 0 (the editor main window) is refused

tools.name: delete_scene_node
tools.description: Delete a node from the edited scene by 'path'. Managed by the editor undo/redo history (action 'Delete Node <name>'): do removes the child and queue_frees it, undo re-adds it under the old parent with owner and sibling index restored — effective while the deferred free has not destroyed the node yet. Refuses to delete the scene root (close the scene first). Returns 'deleted' with 'undoable' true and an 'undo' info object (name, type, parent_path). This tool is classified as a destructive side effect because it destroys a scene entity that already exists in the host, and the editor undo stack is a session-only recovery path that is lost when the editor exits.

path.description: Node path in the edited scene (e.g. 'Enemies/Enemy1'); the scene root cannot be deleted. The response includes scene_path and scene_unsaved to confirm which scene was written

tools.name: detach_script_from_node
tools.description: Remove the script from a node in the edited scene, registered with the editor undo/redo. Requires node_path. Returns 'script detached from <path>'. The node keeps its other properties; attach a new script later with attach_script_to_node. Use it before re-attaching an updated script during iteration.

node_path.description: Node path in the edited scene to detach the script from

tools.name: dotnet_environment
tools.description: Probe the .NET/C# environment of the current project without building anything. Use it before build_csharp_assembly or any C# workflow to learn whether the project is a C# project, whether the dotnet CLI is usable and which SDK version it reports, whether the editor itself is a .NET build, and whether the C# runtime looks loaded. Locates the res:// root .csproj/.sln exactly like build_csharp_assembly, runs 'dotnet --version' synchronously to capture the version string, and decides is_dotnet_editor from the CSharpScript class registration (registered when the .NET module loads) with a version-aware fallback to OS.has_feature(dotnet) on 4.4+ or OS.has_feature(mono) before 4.4 — Godot 4.x registers no mono/dotnet feature tag, so both probes report false. Returns result with dotnet_available, dotnet_version, project_file, is_dotnet_editor, assembly_loaded, engine_version, mono_feature, dotnet_feature and hint; errors when the project is not a C# project or dotnet is not available. On a missing project the error carries a ready-to-write template {path, content, target_framework, assembly_name} derived from the engine version and the installed .NET SDK.

tools.name: drag_input_mouse
tools.description: Drag a point to another point in the editor process by injecting a complete mouse sequence in one call: optional warp to 'from', a motion event, a button press, 'steps' interpolated motion events and a release at 'to'. 'from' and 'to' are objects with numeric x and y fields, in pixels relative to the client area of the focused window — the editor main window while it has focus — not desktop/screen positions. 'button' accepts left, right or middle and defaults to left; 'steps' is the number of interpolated motion events, an integer from 1 to 64 defaulting to 8, and out-of-range values return an error, with the per-step relative delta derived from 'from' and 'to'; 'warp' (default true) moves the physical cursor onto 'from' first. Drag-and-drop depends on the physical mouse and the interpolated path, so the drop may only settle on the next frame — re-observe before concluding that the drag failed. Optional 'observe' (default false) appends a fresh editor viewport capture to the result. A running game is a separate process and will not receive these events. Returns result with ok true.

button.description: Mouse button to drag with: left, right or middle (default: left)

from.description: Drag start position, object with numeric x and y fields, in pixels relative to the client area of the focused window

observe.description: Append a fresh editor viewport capture to the result (default: false)

steps.description: Number of interpolated motion events between from and to, an integer from 1 to 64 (default: 8)

to.description: Drag end position, object with numeric x and y fields, in pixels relative to the client area of the focused window

warp.description: Warp the physical cursor onto the start position first (default: true)

tools.name: duplicate_resource
tools.description: Load a resource from a disk path and return a duplicated instance. deep (default false) controls whether sub-resources are deep-copied. Only file-backed resources are supported; in-memory instances from create_resource must be saved and reloaded first. Pass name to also register the duplicate, so later calls can reference it as memory://name or via the returned object_id; the registered reference is what keeps the duplicate in memory across calls. Returns the duplicate's reference with object_id and name.

deep.description: Deep duplicate copies sub-resources (true), shallow keeps shared references (false, default)

name.description: Registration name so later calls can reference the duplicate as memory://name and via the returned object_id; when omitted only the object_id is registered

path.description: Disk path of the resource to load and duplicate, e.g. res://my_resource.tres; in-memory resources are not supported

tools.name: ensure_directory
tools.description: Create a directory and any missing parents as plain filesystem I/O with no editor resource tracking. Requires 'path' as a res:// or user:// directory below the namespace root (the root itself is rejected). Idempotent: an existing directory succeeds with already_existed true. Returns result (ok), path and already_existed.

path.description: Directory to create below the namespace root (res:// or user://); missing parents are created recursively; idempotent when the directory already exists

tools.name: erase_input_map_action
tools.description: Remove an input action from the editor project InputMap and clear its persisted project setting. The change modifies the editor project InputMap and persists to project settings; a running game process will not see the change until it restarts. Returns 'result' set to 'ok'.

action.description: Action name identifier to remove, e.g. 'mario_jump'; erased from the editor project InputMap and its persisted setting

tools.name: erase_input_map_action_event
tools.description: Remove an input event from an action in the editor project InputMap. 'event_index' is the zero-based index of the event to delete within the action's event list; an out-of-range index returns an error. The change modifies the editor project InputMap and persists to project settings; a running game process will not see the change until it restarts. Returns 'result' set to 'ok'.

action.description: Action name identifier whose event to remove, e.g. 'mario_jump'

event_index.description: Zero-based index of the event to remove within the action's event list

tools.name: execute_game_script
tools.description: Run code or inspect/modify state inside the running game process over the runtime debug channel; requires a game launched from the editor whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension. action is 'script': pass either a complete GDScript defining `func _run()` (used as-is) or bare statements (auto-wrapped into `extends Node` + `func _run()`; explicit `return` needed for a value) — success responses for auto-wrapped sources carry wrapped: true. Unlike execute_script (editor-side, where a single expression auto-returns its value), the game-side eval never auto-returns a bare expression — add an explicit `return`. Other actions are 'get_property', 'set_property' or 'call_method'. persist (default false) keeps the temporary node alive under /root/__gda_runtime and returns its path for later calls; persist_name names it. timeout_ms bounds the in-game execution (default 5000, max 25000; the host waits timeout_ms + 2000 ms, below the 30 s transport timeout); on expiry an idempotent cancel interrupts the pending await and, when the debugger session was breaked, the plugin sends an engine continue so the game is released. call_method on an await method waits for the coroutine to complete (bounded by timeout_ms) and returns its final result; on timeout it returns an error. Optional 'assert' (max 1024 chars) evaluates a sandboxed GDScript expression with the eval result bound as `value` (e.g. "value > 0") and attaches {assert:{pass,expression},actual}: Expression grammar only with no scene access, sharing the op timeout; coroutine (async) results cannot be asserted and fail explicitly — omit assert for awaitable calls. For C# members invisible to GDScript use `csharp_get_property`, `csharp_call_method` and `csharp_subscribe_event` instead (`runtime="game"` forwards over the same runtime channel).

action.description: Action to run in the game process: 'script' (execute arbitrary GDScript), 'get_property', 'set_property' or 'call_method'

assert.description: Optional sandboxed assertion expression (max 1024 chars) evaluated with the eval result bound as value, e.g. value > 0; the response carries assert {pass, expression} plus actual. Expression grammar only with no scene access, sharing the op timeout; coroutine results cannot be asserted — omit assert for awaitable calls

method.description: Method name for call_method; await methods are awaited to completion (bounded by timeout_ms) and return their final result

node_path.description: Node path for get_property/set_property/call_method (omit to use the current scene root)

persist.description: Keep the script's temporary node alive after the call (default: false); the node is stored under /root/__gda_runtime and its path is returned in node_path for later get_property/call_method use

persist_name.description: Node name under /root/__gda_runtime when persist=true (default: auto-generated)

source_code.description: GDScript source for action='script' — a complete script defining func _run() (used as-is), or bare statements auto-wrapped into extends Node + func _run() (an explicit return is needed to produce a value)

timeout_ms.description: Response timeout in milliseconds (default: 5000, max: 25000); on expiry an idempotent cancel interrupts the pending in-game await, and the plugin broadcasts an engine continue when the debugger session was breaked. The host waits timeout_ms + 2000 ms and that budget must stay below the 30 s HTTP transport timeout, so 25000 ms is the hard cap — split long work into shorter calls

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready (gda:ready) before failing; while the game is starting, the request is queued and replayed as soon as readiness arrives. Set false to fail immediately (previous behaviour). Default: true

tools.name: execute_os_process
tools.description: Run an external command and return its exit code, optionally with its stdout and stderr. The process is started without blocking the editor: the editor main thread stays responsive while the call waits for the command to finish on the transport thread, and the pipes are drained frame by frame. Use it for short commands whose result is needed immediately; for long-running or fire-and-forget programs use create_os_process instead. Optional 'timeout_ms' (default 5000, min 100, max 25000) bounds the wait: when the deadline passes the process is terminated and the call fails with code main_thread_timeout (cancelled, not retryable). Returns exit_code, plus stdout and stderr (empty unless 'output' is true); each captured stream is capped at 2 MiB and the result reports stdout_truncated / stderr_truncated with max_output_bytes when the cap was reached. Requires 'path' and 'arguments'.

arguments.description: Command line arguments; non-string entries are ignored

output.description: Capture stdout and stderr into the result (default: false); when false, output is discarded (the pipes are still drained, just not kept in memory). The process is started without blocking the editor and the call waits for it to exit without freezing the editor. Captured output is capped at 2 MiB per stream (GDA_SCAN_MAX_FILE_BYTES): collection stops at the cap and stdout_truncated / stderr_truncated report true alongside max_output_bytes

path.description: Executable to run (full path, or name resolved via PATH)

timeout_ms.description: Deadline for the external process in milliseconds (default: 5000, min: 100, max: 25000); when the deadline passes the process is terminated and the call fails with code main_thread_timeout (cancelled, not retryable)

tools.name: execute_script
tools.description: Execute arbitrary GDScript synchronously in the editor process. Pass the code as either expression or source_code — they are aliases, pass exactly one; providing both is rejected with invalid parameter, and providing neither reports missing required parameter: expression or source_code. Single-expression input returns its value automatically, while multi-line code needs an explicit return statement; this auto-return is editor-side only — execute_game_script never auto-returns a single bare expression and needs an explicit return for a value. print() output appears in the output field, errors in the errors field. Compilation errors include line mapping and the wrapped source. There is no timeout — long code blocks the editor. The environment exposes SceneRoot (edited scene root) for node access; for the running game process use execute_game_script instead.

expression.description: GDScript expression or code to execute; a single expression auto-returns its value. Pass exactly one of expression or source_code (aliases — providing both is rejected)

source_code.description: Alias of expression: GDScript code to execute in the editor process; a single expression auto-returns its value. Pass exactly one of expression or source_code (aliases — providing both is rejected)

tools.name: fill_gridmap_box
tools.description: Fill an axis-aligned cell box on a GridMap node in one call. Requires node_path plus from and to {x, y, z} corner cells (both inclusive; the corner order does not matter). Pass item and optional orientation 0-23 (default 0) to place one item in every cell, or erase=true to clear the box instead (item and orientation are then ignored). The box is capped at 100000 cells per call, so split bigger volumes into chunks. Implemented as a per-cell set_cell_item loop: it saves round trips and produces a single undo action, but does not make the fill itself faster. Returns set_count, from, to, size_x, size_y, size_z and undo.

erase.description: Clear every cell in the box instead of placing items; item and orientation are ignored (default: false)

from.description: Inclusive first corner cell {x, y, z}; the two corners are normalized internally, so from/to order does not matter

item.description: MeshLibrary item id placed in every cell; required and must be >= 0 unless erase is true

node_path.description: Path to the GridMap node

orientation.description: Cell orientation 0-23 placed in every cell (default: 0)

to.description: Inclusive opposite corner cell {x, y, z}

tools.name: fill_tilemap_rect
tools.description: Fill an axis-aligned tile rectangle on a TileMap or TileMapLayer node in one call. Requires node_path plus from and to {x, y} corner cells (both inclusive; the corner order does not matter). Pass source_id and atlas_coords to place one tile in every cell, or erase=true to clear the rect instead (source_id and atlas_coords are then ignored). Optional alternative (default 0) and layer (default 0, TileMapLayer ignores it). The rect is capped at 100000 cells per call, so split bigger areas into chunks. Implemented as a per-cell set_cell/erase_cell loop: it saves a round trip and produces a single undo action, but does not make the fill itself faster. Returns set_count, from, to, width, height and undo.

alternative.description: Alternative tile id placed in every cell (default: 0; must be >= 0)

atlas_coords.description: Atlas coords {x, y} placed in every cell; both must be >= 0 and is required unless erase is true

erase.description: Clear every cell in the rect instead of placing tiles; source_id and atlas_coords are ignored (default: false)

from.description: Inclusive first corner cell {x, y}; the two corners are normalized internally, so from/to order does not matter

layer.description: Tile layer index (default: 0); TileMapLayer nodes ignore it

node_path.description: Path to the TileMap or TileMapLayer node

source_id.description: TileSet source ID placed in every cell; required and must be >= 0 unless erase is true

tools.name: find_docs_class
tools.description: Search all registered Godot classes by case-insensitive substring match on the name. Requires query; returns up to 50 matching classes with name, parent and api_type. Use it before get_docs_class to confirm the exact class name or to discover related classes.

query.description: Search text matched case-insensitively against class names (e.g. 'node' matches Node, Node2D, SceneTree); returns up to 50 matches

tools.name: find_in_files
tools.description: Recursively search text files under a directory (default res://) for a query string, returning each matching file with its occurrence count. Optional 'dir', 'extensions' (array, default gd/tscn/tres/cs/md/json/h/cpp), 'case_sensitive' (default false) and 'max_results' (default 500). Stops early once max_results files are collected and reports truncated: true; the result also carries the files array and total count.

case_sensitive.description: Match the query with case sensitivity (boolean, default: false)

dir.description: Directory to search recursively (string, default: res://)

extensions.description: File extensions to include, without leading dot (array, e.g. ['gd','tscn','cs']); default: ['gd','tscn','tres','cs','md','json','h','cpp']

max_results.description: Maximum number of matching files to return (integer, default: 500); stops searching early and sets truncated: true when exceeded

query.description: Text to search for within each file; files that contain no occurrence are skipped

tools.name: find_render_node_from_rid
tools.description: Check whether an RID is valid and find edited-scene nodes that use it, mainly for debugging render RIDs. Returns rid, is_valid and, when matching nodes exist, a nodes array with node_path and type entries. It is the reverse of get_render_canvas_item_rid. Returns 'ok' even for invalid RIDs.

rid.description: RID to resolve, e.g. from get_render_canvas_item_rid; returns is_valid and matching nodes for debugging

tools.name: find_unused_resources
tools.description: Find project files that are never referenced by any other file's dependencies under 'directory' (optional string, default "res://", e.g. "res://assets"). Scans the editor filesystem recursively (EditorFileSystemDirectory), collects each file's get_dependencies(), resolves uid:// entries through ResourceUID (unresolvable ones are listed in 'unresolved_uids' instead of being misreported), then subtracts the referenced set plus exemptions: icon.svg, main_scene and autoload paths read from ProjectSettings, *.import sidecars and project.godot. Returns {scanned, unused:[{path,type}], unresolved_uids, exempted}. Read-only; large projects may take a few seconds.

directory.description: Project directory whose files are scanned recursively for unreferenced resources (string, default: "res://", e.g. "res://assets")

tools.name: focus_camera_on_node
tools.description: Point a scene camera at a node: pass 'camera_path' (a Camera2D for 2D targets, a Camera3D for 3D targets) and 'target_path' (Node2D or Control for 2D cameras, Node3D for 3D cameras; other types error naming the actual class). A 2D camera is centered on the target anchor (the Control global-rect center, otherwise the canvas origin) and reports the padded 'focus_rect'; a 3D camera keeps its position and turns toward the target via look_at, reporting whether the target is 'behind' it. Optional 'margin' (number, default 0, must not be negative) grows the 2D focus rect, or pulls a 3D camera back along its view direction before aiming. One editor undo step; marks the scene modified. Returns camera and target paths and types, space, position, zoom and focus_rect (2D) or target_position and behind (3D), plus margin.

camera_path.description: Camera node path in the edited scene (a Camera2D for 2D targets, a Camera3D for 3D targets)

margin.description: Extra padding: grows the 2D focus rect around the target anchor, or pulls a 3D camera back along its view direction by this many world units (number, default: 0, must not be negative)

target_path.description: Target node path in the edited scene to focus on (Node2D or Control for 2D cameras, Node3D for 3D cameras)

tools.name: get_animation_list
tools.description: List every animation of the AnimationPlayer at 'player_path' (required string) with per-animation metadata: 'length' in seconds and 'loop_mode' (0 none / 1 linear / 2 pingpong). Read-only; returns {player_path, count, animations:[{name,length,loop_mode}]}. Errors if the node is not an AnimationPlayer.

player_path.description: Path of the AnimationPlayer node in the edited scene

tools.name: get_audio_bus_count
tools.description: Get the number of audio buses currently defined, including the default Master bus which always occupies index 0. Use the returned count to bound 'bus_index' values passed to the other bus tools. Returns the count as an integer in 'result'.

tools.name: get_audio_bus_layout
tools.description: Get the complete audio bus layout from the audio server, including the Master bus and every bus effect chain. Use this to inspect the current bus routing or to snapshot a layout before making changes. Returns the serialized AudioBusLayout object in 'result'. No parameters are required.

tools.name: get_audio_bus_name
tools.description: Get the name of an audio bus by its zero-based index. Index 0 is always the Master bus, and the index must be smaller than the count returned by get_audio_bus_count or an error is returned. Returns the bus name string in 'result'.

bus_index.description: Zero-based audio bus index; 0 is the Master bus and the index must be below the count from get_audio_bus_count

tools.name: get_audio_device_inputs
tools.description: List the audio input devices available on this machine, such as microphones. Use the returned device name strings directly as the 'device' value for set_audio_device_input. Returns an array of device name strings in 'result'. The list reflects hardware attached to the system, not project settings.

tools.name: get_audio_device_outputs
tools.description: List the audio output devices available on this machine, such as speakers and headphones. Use the returned device name strings directly as the 'device' value for set_audio_device_output. Returns an array of device name strings in 'result'. The list reflects hardware attached to the system, not project settings.

tools.name: get_audio_input_devices
tools.description: List the audio input devices available on this machine, such as microphones, together with the current capture state. Use a returned device name as the 'device' value for start_audio_input_capture or set_audio_device_input. Returns an object with 'devices' (array of device name strings), 'current', 'input_mix_rate' and 'frames_available' in 'result'.

tools.name: get_audio_player_playback_position
tools.description: Get the current playback position of an audio player node in seconds. 'node_path' is a scene-relative path such as 'Level1/Player' or an absolute '/root/...' path, and must resolve to an AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStreamPlayer2D or AudioStreamPlayer3D. Returns the position as a float in 'result'.

node_path.description: Scene-relative path to an AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStreamPlayer2D or AudioStreamPlayer3D node, e.g. 'Level1/Player' or absolute '/root/Level1/Player'

tools.name: get_autoload_list
tools.description: List all autoload singletons registered in the project configuration (project.godot) in load order. Each entry carries name, path (the res:// target with the leading * singleton marker stripped), enabled (whether the * marker is present) and order. Read-only; change the list with add_autoload, remove_autoload or move_autoload. Returns the entries in result plus count.

tools.name: get_camera_view_rect
tools.description: Describe what a scene camera sees in editor window client-area coordinates with the same mapping as get_scene_node_screen_rect (client = offset + pixel * scale). Pass 'camera_path' (a Camera2D or Camera3D; other types error naming the actual class). Returns camera_path, camera_type, viewport, window_id, space, world_position, window_center, 'view_rect' ({position, size} centered on the projected camera origin with the editor viewport size), 'behind' (always false for 2D; true when a 3D camera origin sits behind the 3D editor camera), zoom (2D) or forward, fov, near and far (3D), viewport_size and the pixel mapping. Read-only.

camera_path.description: Camera node path in the edited scene (Camera2D or Camera3D)

tools.name: get_curve_baked_points
tools.description: Read the baked polyline of a curve created by create_curve_resource without modifying it. Requires name (the memory:// reference). Returns points as an array of {x, y} (Curve2D) or {x, y, z} (Curve3D) objects with count, baked_length, class and name. Read-only.

name.description: Registration name of a curve from create_curve_resource (memory://name)

tools.name: get_debug_custom_monitor
tools.description: Read the current value of a custom performance monitor by its string id. Use it after registering a monitor with Performance.add_custom_monitor from game code or scripts. Returns the monitor value serialized as JSON Variant, whose shape depends on what the registration returned.

id.description: Name of the custom monitor to read, as registered via Performance.add_custom_monitor; the value is serialized as JSON Variant

tools.name: get_debug_custom_monitor_names
tools.description: List the names of all registered custom performance monitors. Use it to discover monitor ids before calling get_debug_custom_monitor or to verify that game code registered the expected monitors. Returns an array of name strings; takes no parameters. The list is empty when no custom monitor is registered.

tools.name: get_debug_memory_usage
tools.description: Read current static memory usage in bytes from the Performance singleton. Use it to observe memory growth trends while running scripted tests. Returns a byte count as a number; takes no parameters. Note it reflects static engine memory only, not GPU or texture memory.

tools.name: get_debug_monitor
tools.description: Read the current value of one built-in performance monitor by integer id. Look up the id with get_debug_monitor_catalog first; ids outside the catalog range return an error. Returns the monitor value as a number; for a snapshot of all monitors use get_debug_monitors instead.

monitor.description: Performance monitor ID (integer 0-58); list valid ids with get_debug_monitor_catalog first. Out-of-range ids return an error

tools.name: get_debug_monitor_catalog
tools.description: List all built-in performance monitors with their catalog id, name and type (time, memory or quantity). Use it to find valid ids for get_debug_monitor before querying values. Returns an array of {id, name, type} entries; takes no parameters and is the authoritative source of monitor ids.

tools.name: get_debug_monitors
tools.description: Read current values of all built-in performance monitors in one call. Use it for a full performance snapshot without repeated get_debug_monitor calls. Returns an array of {name, type, value} entries covering 59 monitors; takes no parameters. Values are captured at the moment of the call.

tools.name: get_debug_node_count
tools.description: Read the current live Node count from the Performance singleton. Use it with get_debug_object_count to detect node leaks by comparing counts before and after scene operations or scripted loops. Returns the count as a number and takes no parameters; a steadily rising count suggests leaked nodes.

tools.name: get_debug_object_count
tools.description: Read the total live Object count from the Performance singleton. Use it to detect object leaks by comparing counts before and after a scripted operation; pair it with get_debug_node_count for node-specific counts. Returns the count as a number; takes no parameters.

tools.name: get_debug_object_info
tools.description: Resolve an object instance ID (ObjectID) to its class and identity. Use it with object IDs obtained from scene or physics tools to identify what an object is. Returns result 'ok', class (Godot class name), name and node_path (for Nodes), plus resource_path (for Resources); errors out if the ID is stale or invalid.

object_id.description: Object instance ID (ObjectID) to resolve, as returned by scene or physics tools; looked up in ObjectDB. Returns class, name, node_path (Node) or resource_path (Resource)

tools.name: get_debug_stack
tools.description: Capture script backtraces for all currently running scripts in the editor process. Use it when a script error occurs to see where execution was at capture time; it needs no debug session. Returns per-backtrace language and frame_count, with frames containing function, file and line; include_variables adds global_variables per backtrace plus local_variables and member_variables per frame.

include_variables.description: Include variable names in the dump: global_variables per backtrace, local_variables and member_variables per frame (default: false)

tools.name: get_debugger_errors
tools.description: Read script errors from the running game process as a structured list (time, file, func, line, error, descr, is_warning, stack, seq). Requires a game launched from the editor (play_editor_current_scene) whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension; without an active debug session it returns an empty result plus a note — no editor-side fallback. Use get_debugger_log for script errors and output of the editor process instead. Optional 'limit' (default 20) caps the result; with an active session it caps raw entries (ungrouped) or returned groups (grouped). Ungrouped responses over the runtime channel keep the raw list under result and carry next_seq as its top-level sibling; optional 'group' (default false) clusters entries by file/function/line/message and returns {grouped:true, groups:[{count,first_time,last_time,file,func,line,error,descr,is_warning,stack,last_seq}], total_errors, total_groups, next_seq} as response top-level keys instead. Optional 'since_seq' (integer, exclusive) returns only entries with seq > since_seq, and the response carries the top-level next_seq — start with 0 and pass the previous next_seq to read only new errors.

limit.description: Maximum number of errors to return (default: 20); with an active debug session the raw list is returned under the response's result key (each entry carries time, file, func, line, error, descr, is_warning, stack, seq) with next_seq as its top-level sibling, otherwise an empty result plus a note — no editor-side fallback; use get_debugger_log for editor-process script errors and output

since_seq.description: Only return errors with seq > since_seq (exclusive lower bound, incremental read); start with 0 and pass the response's top-level next_seq on the next call to fetch only new entries — over the runtime channel next_seq is a top-level response key in both the grouped and the ungrouped shape (the no-session editor-side fallback has neither seq nor next_seq). Each raw entry carries seq, each grouped entry carries last_seq, and next_seq is the highest seq this response covers (the current game error sequence when nothing matched). Omit it to keep the previous tail-of-buffer behaviour

tools.name: get_debugger_log
tools.description: Read the editor-process engine log buffer, including script errors and print output routed through the engine logger. It always contains data and does not require a running game; for the running game use get_debugger_errors, and for the game process log file on disk use get_game_log_entries. Optional 'limit' (default 50) caps the returned entries.

limit.description: Maximum number of log entries to return (default: 50); the most recent entries are kept. The buffer always has data from the editor process engine logger, even without a running game

tools.name: get_debugger_output
tools.description: Read stdout/stderr output captured from the running game process over the runtime channel. Requires a game launched from the editor (play_editor_current_scene) whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension; without an active debug session it returns an empty result plus a note — no editor-side fallback. For editor-process output use get_debugger_log; to read the game process log file use get_game_log_entries. Optional 'limit' (default 50) caps the result.

limit.description: Maximum number of output entries to return (default: 50); fetched from the running game over the runtime channel when a debug session is active, otherwise an empty result plus a note — no editor-side fallback; use get_debugger_log for editor-process output or get_game_log_entries to read the game process log file

tools.name: get_debugger_scene_tree
tools.description: Read the scene tree of the running game process (node names and types) over the runtime channel. Requires a game launched from the editor (play_editor_current_scene) whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension; without an active debug session it returns an empty result plus a note — no editor-side fallback. Returns a formatted text tree; takes no parameters.

tools.name: get_debugger_session_info
tools.description: Read the current debug session state of the editor debugger. Use it to check whether a game is running (active) or stopped at a breakpoint (breaked) before using other debugger tools. Returns a text summary with active, breaked, running and session count; takes no parameters.

tools.name: get_display_clipboard
tools.description: Read the current text contents of the system clipboard. Use it to retrieve text copied from other applications or previously set with set_display_clipboard. Returns result as a string; it may be empty when the clipboard holds no text or only non-text data.

tools.name: get_display_mouse_position
tools.description: Return the current mouse cursor position in screen (desktop) coordinates — a different basis from warp_display_mouse and the mouse input tools, whose positions are relative to the client area of the focused window.
