space.description: Transform space: 'local' (default) writes the values directly to position/rotation/scale; 'global' interprets them in world space and converts to local via the parent global transform

tools.name: set_os_environment
tools.description: Set an environment variable in the editor process environment. Use it to influence the editor or child processes started afterwards, for example to override tooling paths; the change is not persisted and only affects the current session. Requires 'variable' and 'value' (strings); returns result 'ok'.

variable.description: Environment variable name to set in the editor process environment; the change is session-only and not persisted

tools.name: set_particles_params
tools.description: Set playback parameters on a particle node in the edited scene. Pass the node path of a GPUParticles2D, GPUParticles3D, CPUParticles2D or CPUParticles3D node; all value parameters are optional and only the given ones are applied: emitting toggles emission, amount sets the particle count, lifetime sets seconds per particle, one_shot selects single-burst emission, speed_scale scales playback speed and explosiveness sets the burst ratio. Returns 'ok'. Errors if the node is missing, is not a particle node, or a value has the wrong type.

amount.description: Particle amount, number of particles in the system

emitting.description: Emit particles, true starts and false stops emission

explosiveness.description: Explosiveness ratio 0.0-1.0, higher values emit particles together at the start (default: 0.0)

lifetime.description: Particle lifetime in seconds; controls how long each particle stays alive (default: 1.0)

one_shot.description: One-shot emission, true emits once then stops (default: false)

path.description: Node path of a GPUParticles2D, GPUParticles3D, CPUParticles2D or CPUParticles3D node in the edited scene; example: 'Level1/Sparks' (leading slash and root/ prefix are tolerated)

speed_scale.description: Speed scale multiplier for particle playback (default: 1.0)

tools.name: set_physics_2d_area_monitorable
tools.description: Set whether a 2D physics area can be monitored by other areas, controlling overlap detection between areas. Requires rid and monitorable; with monitorable false, other areas will not receive overlap events involving this area, while bodies are unaffected. Returns 'ok' or an error for invalid RIDs

monitorable.description: Required. True lets other areas monitor this area for overlap detection; bodies are unaffected

rid.description: Required. RID of the 2D physics area, e.g. from create_physics_2d_area

tools.name: set_physics_2d_body_mode
tools.description: Set the simulation mode of a 2D physics body created by create_physics_2d_body. Requires rid and mode: 0=static, 1=kinematic, 2=rigid, 3=rigid_linear. Only rigid modes respond to forces and impulses from the apply_physics_2d_body_* tools. Returns 'ok' or an error for invalid RIDs and out-of-range modes

mode.description: Required. Body mode enum index: 0=static, 1=kinematic, 2=rigid, 3=rigid_linear; only rigid modes react to forces and impulses

rid.description: Required. RID of the 2D physics body, e.g. from create_physics_2d_body

tools.name: set_physics_2d_body_state
tools.description: Set a state field on a 2D physics body, such as its transform or velocity. Requires rid, state and value; state selects the field: 0=transform, 1=linear_vel, 2=angular_vel, 3=sleeping, 4=can_sleep, and value must match (transform object, Vector2 or boolean). Pair with get_physics_2d_body_state to read the same fields. Returns 'ok' or an error for invalid state values

rid.description: Required. RID of the 2D physics body, e.g. from create_physics_2d_body

value.description: Required. New state value matching the state: a transform object (origin/rotation/scale) for 0, a Vector2 object for 1 and 2, a boolean for 3 and 4

tools.name: set_physics_2d_shape_data
tools.description: Set the geometric data of a 2D circle shape RID, configuring its size for physics queries. Requires rid and data, where data is an object such as {'radius': 10} for a circle. Use after create_physics_2d_circle_shape and before intersect_physics_2d_shape so the query uses the correct dimensions. Returns 'ok' or an error for missing parameters

data.description: Required. Shape geometry object, e.g. {'radius': 10} for a circle

rid.description: Required. RID of the 2D shape, e.g. from create_physics_2d_circle_shape

tools.name: set_physics_3d_area_monitorable
tools.description: Set whether a 3D physics area can be monitored by other areas, controlling overlap detection between areas. Requires rid and monitorable; with monitorable false, other areas will not receive overlap events involving this area, while bodies are unaffected. Returns 'ok' or an error for invalid RIDs

monitorable.description: Required. True lets other areas monitor this area for overlap detection; bodies are unaffected

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics area, e.g. from create_physics_3d_area

tools.name: set_physics_3d_area_param
tools.description: Set a physics parameter on a 3D area by enum index, such as gravity, damping or priority. Requires rid, param and value; param is a number matching the engine's AreaParameter enum (0=gravity_override_mode, 1=gravity, 2=gravity_vector, 3=gravity_is_point, 4=gravity_point_unit_distance, 5=linear_damp_override_mode, 6=linear_damp, 7=angular_damp_override_mode, 8=angular_damp, 9=priority), and value matches the parameter's type (number, Vector3 object or boolean). Returns 'ok' or an error for invalid RIDs

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics area, e.g. from create_physics_3d_area

value.description: Required. Value matching the selected parameter: a number for scalar params (e.g. gravity, damp), a Vector3 object like {'x': 0, 'y': -9.8, 'z': 0} for vectors, or a boolean

tools.name: set_physics_3d_area_space
tools.description: Attach a 3D area to a physics space (area_set_space semantics). Requires rid of the area and space_rid of the target space; the area then interacts with bodies and other areas in that space. Use this to move an area between spaces or to attach one created by create_physics_3d_area to a specific space. Returns 'ok' or an error when either RID is invalid

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D area, e.g. from create_physics_3d_area

space_rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics space to attach the area to; the area then interacts with bodies and areas in that space

tools.name: set_physics_3d_area_transform
tools.description: Set the global transform of a 3D physics area, placing its detection volume in the space. Requires rid and transform (Transform3D with basis array and origin). Use this after create_physics_3d_area to position the area where it should detect overlaps. Returns 'ok' or an error when the transform is missing

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics area, e.g. from create_physics_3d_area

transform.description: Required. Transform3D as an object with basis (array of 3 row arrays, each with 3 numbers) and origin (Vector3 object with x, y and z)

tools.name: set_physics_3d_body_axis_lock
tools.description: Lock or unlock a single movement axis on a 3D physics body, restricting its freedom of motion. Requires rid, axis and lock; axis is a bit flag: 1=linear_x, 2=linear_y, 4=linear_z, 8=angular_x, 16=angular_y, 32=angular_z, and lock is true to lock or false to unlock. Works on bodies created by create_physics_3d_body. Returns 'ok' or an error for invalid axis values

axis.description: Required. Axis bit flag: 1=linear_x, 2=linear_y, 4=linear_z, 8=angular_x, 16=angular_y, 32=angular_z; only one flag per call

lock.description: Required. True locks the axis, false unlocks it

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics body, e.g. from create_physics_3d_body

tools.name: set_physics_3d_body_mode
tools.description: Set the simulation mode of a 3D physics body created by create_physics_3d_body. Requires rid and mode: 0=static, 1=kinematic, 2=rigid, 3=rigid_linear. Only rigid modes respond to forces, impulses and torque from the apply_physics_3d_body_* tools. Returns 'ok' or an error for invalid RIDs and out-of-range modes

mode.description: Required. Body mode enum index: 0=static, 1=kinematic, 2=rigid, 3=rigid_linear; only rigid modes react to forces and impulses

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics body, e.g. from create_physics_3d_body

tools.name: set_physics_3d_body_param
tools.description: Set a physics parameter on a 3D body by enum index, such as mass, friction or gravity scale. Requires rid, param and value; param is a number matching the engine's BodyParameter enum (0=bounce, 1=friction, 2=mass, 3=inertia, 4=center_of_mass, 5=gravity_scale, 6=linear_damp_mode, 7=angular_damp_mode, 8=linear_damp, 9=angular_damp), and value is the numeric setting. Returns 'ok' or an error for invalid RIDs

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics body, e.g. from create_physics_3d_body

value.description: Required. Numeric value for the selected parameter, e.g. 0.5 for friction

tools.name: set_physics_3d_body_state
tools.description: Set a state field on a 3D physics body, such as its transform or velocity. Requires rid, state and value; state selects the field: 0=transform, 1=linear_vel, 2=angular_vel, 3=sleeping, 4=can_sleep, and value must match (transform object, Vector3 or boolean). Pair with get_physics_3d_body_state to read the same fields. Returns 'ok' or an error for invalid state values

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics body, e.g. from create_physics_3d_body

value.description: Required. New state value matching the state: a transform object (basis/origin) for 0, a Vector3 object for 1 and 2, a boolean for 3 and 4

tools.name: set_physics_3d_body_transform
tools.description: Set the global transform of a 3D physics body, teleporting it in the space. Requires rid and transform (Transform3D with basis array and origin). Use this on bodies created by create_physics_3d_body to place them before simulation or to snap them to a new pose. Returns 'ok' or an error when the transform is missing

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics body, e.g. from create_physics_3d_body

transform.description: Required. New body transform: object with basis (array of 3 row arrays) and origin (Vector3 object); sets the body's global transform directly

tools.name: set_physics_3d_joint_param
tools.description: Set a parameter on a 3D physics joint created by create_physics_3d_joint. Requires rid and at least one of solver_priority (integer, higher values solve the joint first) or disable_collision (boolean, stops the two jointed bodies from colliding); both are optional, and only the ones supplied are applied. Returns 'ok' or an error for invalid RIDs

disable_collision.description: Optional. True disables collisions between the two jointed bodies

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D joint, e.g. from create_physics_3d_joint

solver_priority.description: Optional. Integer priority for solver order; higher values solve the joint first

tools.name: set_physics_3d_shape_data
tools.description: Set the geometric data of a sphere shape RID, configuring its size for physics queries. Requires rid and data, where data is an object such as {'radius': 0.5} for a sphere. Use after create_physics_3d_sphere_shape and before queries such as intersect_physics_3d_shape so the shape has the correct dimensions. Returns 'ok' or an error for missing parameters

data.description: Required. Shape geometry object, e.g. {'radius': 0.5} for a sphere

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D shape, e.g. from create_physics_3d_sphere_shape

tools.name: set_physics_3d_soft_body_mesh
tools.description: Set the mesh of a 3D soft body, defining the surface that deforms under physics forces. Requires rid of the soft body from create_physics_3d_soft_body and mesh_rid of the mesh to assign. The mesh must be created or loaded before calling this. Returns 'ok' or an error when either RID is invalid

mesh_rid.description: Required. RID id of the mesh to assign to the soft body

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D soft body, e.g. from create_physics_3d_soft_body

tools.name: set_physics_3d_space_param
tools.description: Set a physics parameter on a 3D space by enum index, such as solver iterations or penetration limits. Requires space_rid, param and value; param is a number matching the engine's SpaceParameter enum (0=contact_recycle_radius, 1=contact_max_separation, 2=contact_max_allowed_penetration, 3=contact_default_bias, 4=body_linear_velocity_sleep_threshold, 5=body_angular_velocity_sleep_threshold, 6=body_time_to_sleep, 7=solver_iterations), and value is the numeric setting. Returns 'ok' or an error for invalid RIDs

space_rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics space

value.description: Required. Numeric value for the selected parameter

tools.name: set_physics_3d_space_solver_iterations
tools.description: Set the solver iterations of a 3D physics space, trading simulation accuracy for performance. Requires rid; higher solver_iterations values improve constraint accuracy but cost more CPU. This does not change gravity itself: actual gravity is configured through set_physics_3d_area_param or the project's physics settings. Returns 'ok' or an error for invalid RIDs

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics space

solver_iterations.description: Optional. Number of solver iterations (integer); higher values improve accuracy at higher CPU cost. Does not change gravity itself

tools.name: set_physics_3d_space_solver_params
tools.description: Set solver parameters on a 3D physics space: solver_iterations and contact_max_allowed_penetration. Requires rid; solver_iterations (integer) controls constraint accuracy, while contact_max_allowed_penetration (number) sets how deep bodies may overlap before the solver corrects them. Both are optional and applied only when supplied. Returns 'ok' or an error for invalid RIDs

contact_max_allowed_penetration.description: Optional. Maximum allowed penetration depth (number) before the solver pushes bodies apart

rid.description: Required. RID of the 3D physics space

solver_iterations.description: Optional. Number of solver iterations (integer); higher values improve constraint accuracy at higher CPU cost

tools.name: set_physics_body_bundle
tools.description: Create a physics body together with its collision shape and parameters in one call: creates (or reuses) the body, creates the shape, attaches it with body_add_shape and applies mode, layer, mask, mass, friction and bounce. Required 'dimension' is '2d' (PhysicsServer2D) or '3d' (PhysicsServer3D); required 'body_type' is 'static', 'kinematic', 'rigid' or 'rigid_linear' (optional numeric 'mode' 0-3 overrides it). Required 'shape' carries 'type' plus dimensions: 2D 'circle' with radius, 'rectangle' with full-extent size {x, y}, 'capsule' with radius and height; 3D 'sphere' with radius, 'box' with full-extent size {x, y, z}, 'capsule' with radius and height; the type must belong to the requested dimension. Omit both 'body_rid' and 'node_path' to create a new server body, pass 'body_rid' to reuse an existing body handle, or pass 'node_path' to configure the server body of a CollisionObject2D (2d) or CollisionObject3D (3d) in the edited scene; 'body_rid' and 'node_path' are mutually exclusive. The returned body_rid and shape_rid are physics-server handles: a shape RID cannot be assigned directly to CollisionShape2D.shape or CollisionShape3D.shape, which expect Shape2D/Shape3D resources, so bridge through save_resource plus set_property instead, and use the RIDs with the intersect_physics_* and set_physics_* server tools. Returns 'body_rid', 'shape_rid' and 'params_applied'.

body_rid.description: Optional. Existing body handle to reuse instead of creating one; mutually exclusive with 'node_path'

body_type.description: Required. Body mode name: 'static', 'kinematic', 'rigid' or 'rigid_linear'; overridden by numeric 'mode' when both are given

bounce.description: Optional. Body bounce applied via body_set_param; must be >= 0

dimension.description: Required. Physics dimension: '2d' uses PhysicsServer2D, '3d' uses PhysicsServer3D; the shape type and the node_path node type must belong to it

friction.description: Optional. Body friction applied via body_set_param; must be >= 0

layer.description: Optional. Collision layer bitfield applied via body_set_collision_layer

mask.description: Optional. Collision mask bitfield applied via body_set_collision_mask

mass.description: Optional. Body mass applied via body_set_param; must be positive

mode.description: Optional. Numeric BodyMode 0=static, 1=kinematic, 2=rigid, 3=rigid_linear; overrides 'body_type' when given

node_path.description: Optional. Scene path of a CollisionObject2D (dimension '2d') or CollisionObject3D (dimension '3d') whose server body is configured; mutually exclusive with 'body_rid'

shape.description: Required. Shape description with 'type' plus dimensions: 2D 'circle' {radius}, 'rectangle' {size {x, y} full extents}, 'capsule' {radius, height}; 3D 'sphere' {radius}, 'box' {size {x, y, z} full extents}, 'capsule' {radius, height}

tools.name: set_project_settings
tools.description: Set a project setting in memory. Note: the change is NOT written to project.godot automatically, so call save_project_settings afterwards or the setting is lost when the editor closes. value is a serialized JSON value; the engine keeps the existing type when known. Differs from set_editor_settings, which persists automatically. Returns ok.

name.description: Project setting name, e.g. application/config/name; must already exist or be added by this call

value.description: Serialized JSON value; when a string, the engine keeps the existing setting's type if one is stored, e.g. 1920 for an int setting

tools.name: set_properties_batch
tools.description: Set many properties on one scene node in a single undo step. Requires 'path' and 'properties' as an object map (max 32 entries after slash-family expansion); 'atomic' (boolean, default true) selects all-or-nothing rollback versus best-effort partial success. Object-typed entries apply first, then the rest, mirroring property_set. Each entry uses the same strict conversion chain as property_set (resource references resolved, NodePath strings become node references, arrays converted per element, inline resource descriptions create pathless sub-resources, slash families expand per item). Each entry is read back and rejected values restore the old value. All applied entries share one editor undo action; object-typed values report undoable:false with a reason. Returns applied_properties, property_warnings ({path, property, warning} only when the engine adjusted a value), failed ([{property, error}] empty on full success, non-empty on atomic:false partial success), undo ([{path, property, old_value}]) plus undoable state. Entries starting with 'metadata/' address node metadata with the same key rules as property_set, stored directly from JSON without type checks and rolled back atomically with the rest.

atomic.description: When true (default) the batch is all-or-nothing: first failure rolls back already applied entries and returns an error; when false best-effort partial success is returned with applied_properties plus failed entries

path.description: Node path in the edited scene (string, e.g. 'Player' or 'Player/Camera2D')

properties.description: Batch map of property names to values applied in one call (e.g. {"position": {"x": 1, "y": 2}, "visible": false}). Object-typed entries run first, then the rest, mirroring property_set batch; slash families accept an object of suffixes; max 32 entries after expansion

tools.name: set_render_camera_orthogonal
tools.description: Set an orthogonal projection on a camera, typically for 2D-like or UI rendering. Pass the RID from create_render_camera; size defaults to 10, z_near to 0.01 and z_far to 4000. Objects keep their size regardless of distance. Returns 'ok'. Errors if camera_rid is missing.

camera_rid.description: RID of the render camera, from create_render_camera

z_far.description: Far clip distance, objects beyond it are culled (default: 4000)

z_near.description: Near clip distance, keep small but positive (default: 0.01)

tools.name: set_render_camera_perspective
tools.description: Set a perspective (frustum) projection on a camera. Pass the RID from create_render_camera; fovy_degrees defaults to 75, z_near to 0.01 and z_far to 4000. Use it for natural 3D scenes where objects shrink with distance. Returns 'ok'. Errors if camera_rid is missing.

camera_rid.description: RID of the render camera, from create_render_camera

fovy_degrees.description: Vertical field of view in degrees (default: 75); example: 60

z_far.description: Far clip distance, objects beyond it are culled (default: 4000)

z_near.description: Near clip distance, keep small but positive (default: 0.01)

tools.name: set_render_camera_transform
tools.description: Set the 3D camera position. Pass the RID from create_render_camera; only the origin is applied, rotation and scale stay at identity, so the camera always looks down -Z. Combine with set_render_camera_perspective or set_render_camera_orthogonal to define the view frustum. Returns 'ok'. Errors if camera_rid is missing.

camera_rid.description: RID of the render camera, from create_render_camera

tools.name: set_render_canvas_item_transform
tools.description: Set the 2D transform of a canvas item: x and y scale the local axes, origin_x and origin_y offset the position. Pass the RID from create_render_canvas_item. All parameters are optional and default to identity. Returns 'ok'. Errors if canvas_item_rid is missing.

canvas_item_rid.description: RID of the canvas item, from create_render_canvas_item

tools.name: set_render_canvas_item_visible
tools.description: Set the visibility state of a canvas item, not a toggle. Pass the RID from create_render_canvas_item; visible defaults to true. Hide the item to remove its draw commands from the canvas temporarily; set it back to true to restore drawing. Returns 'ok'. Errors if canvas_item_rid is missing.

canvas_item_rid.description: RID of the canvas item, from create_render_canvas_item

visible.description: Visibility state, true shows and false hides (default: true)

tools.name: set_render_environment_ambient_light
tools.description: Set the ambient light of an environment. Pass the environment RID from an external source (e.g. code_execute); source selects 0=bg, 1=disabled, 2=color, 3=sky and energy scales brightness. Ambient light fills shadows so unlit surfaces stay visible. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

color.description: Ambient light color {r, g, b, a}, each in 0.0-1.0

environment_rid.description: RID of the render environment; must come from an external source (e.g. code_execute), as no create tool exists

tools.name: set_render_environment_bg_color
tools.description: Set the background color of an environment. Pass the environment RID from an external source (e.g. code_execute); no create tool exists. Requires a color {r, g, b, a}. It takes effect when the environment background mode is set to color. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

color.description: Background color {r, g, b, a}, each in 0.0-1.0; example: {r: 0.1, g: 0.2, b: 0.4, a: 1}

environment_rid.description: RID of the render environment; must come from an external source (e.g. code_execute), as no create tool exists

tools.name: set_render_environment_glow
tools.description: Configure glow (bloom) post-processing on an environment. Pass the environment RID from an external source (e.g. code_execute); all parameters are optional, see schema for meanings and defaults. Glow makes bright areas bleed into their surroundings. Returns 'ok'. Errors if environment_rid is missing.

environment_rid.description: RID of the render environment; must come from an external source (e.g. code_execute), as no create tool exists

tools.name: set_render_environment_sdfgi
tools.description: Configure SDFGI global illumination on an environment. Pass the environment RID from an external source (e.g. code_execute); all parameters are optional, see schema for meanings and defaults. SDFGI provides GI for large outdoor scenes. Returns 'ok'. Errors if environment_rid is missing.

environment_rid.description: RID of the render environment; must come from an external source (e.g. code_execute), as no create tool exists

tools.name: set_render_environment_ssr
tools.description: Configure screen-space reflections on an environment. Pass the environment RID from an external source (e.g. code_execute); all parameters are optional, see schema for meanings and defaults. SSR reflects visible geometry onto reflective surfaces without cubemaps. Returns 'ok'. Errors if environment_rid is missing.

environment_rid.description: RID of the render environment; must come from an external source (e.g. code_execute), as no create tool exists

tools.name: set_render_environment_tonemap
tools.description: Configure tone mapping and exposure on an environment. Pass the environment RID from an external source (e.g. code_execute); tone_mapper, exposure and white are optional, see schema for meanings. Tone mapping maps HDR scene colors to the display range. Returns 'ok'. Errors if environment_rid is missing.

environment_rid.description: RID of the render environment; must come from an external source (e.g. code_execute), as no create tool exists

exposure.description: Exposure, higher values brighten the image (default: 1.0)

white.description: White reference in ev; higher values darken highlights (default: 1.0)

tools.name: set_render_environment_volumetric_fog
tools.description: Configure volumetric fog on an environment. Pass the environment RID from an external source (e.g. code_execute); all parameters are optional, see schema for meanings and defaults. It fills the scene with light-scattering fog, e.g. mist or smoke. Returns 'ok'. Errors if environment_rid is missing.

albedo.description: Fog albedo color {r, g, b, a}, each in 0.0-1.0

density.description: Fog density, higher makes fog thicker (default: 0.05)

emission.description: Fog emission color {r, g, b, a}, each in 0.0-1.0

environment_rid.description: RID of the render environment; must come from an external source (e.g. code_execute), as no create tool exists

tools.name: set_render_fog_volume_shape
tools.description: Set the shape of a fog volume after creation. Pass the fog RID from create_render_fog_volume; the same shape can also be supplied at creation. Different shapes suit different fog layouts, e.g. ellipsoid for clouds. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

fog_rid.description: RID of the fog volume, from create_render_fog_volume

tools.name: set_render_instance_layer_mask
tools.description: Set the layer mask of a rendering instance, controlling which camera layers see it. The instance RID must come from an external source (e.g. code_execute), as no create tool exists; mask is a bitfield. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

instance_rid.description: RID of the render instance; must come from an external source (e.g. code_execute), as no create tool exists

mask.description: Layer mask bitfield; bit n selects layer n+1, example: 1 for layer 1, 3 for layers 1 and 2

tools.name: set_render_instance_visible
tools.description: Set the visibility state of a rendering instance, not a toggle. The instance RID must come from an external source (e.g. code_execute), as no create tool exists; visible defaults to true. Use it to show or hide a server-side object in the rendered scene. Returns 'ok'. Errors if instance_rid is missing.

instance_rid.description: RID of the render instance; must come from an external source (e.g. code_execute), as no create tool exists

visible.description: Visibility state, true shows and false hides (default: true)

tools.name: set_render_light_color
tools.description: Set the color of a light. Pass the RID from create_render_light and a color {r, g, b, a}; alpha is ignored. Combine with set_render_light_param to control energy and range. Lights tint the surfaces they illuminate. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

color.description: Light color {r, g, b, a}, each in 0.0-1.0; alpha is ignored, example: {r: 1, g: 0.9, b: 0.7, a: 1}

light_rid.description: RID of the render light, from create_render_light

tools.name: set_render_light_param
tools.description: Set a numeric parameter on a light. Pass the RID from create_render_light, a param index (0=energy, 1=specular, 2=range, 3=size, 4=attenuation) and a float value. Which parameters apply depends on the light type, e.g. range only affects omni and spot lights. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

light_rid.description: RID of the render light, from create_render_light

value.description: Parameter value; units depend on param, e.g. range is in meters

tools.name: set_render_material_param
tools.description: Set a named parameter on a material. Pass the RID from create_render_material, the parameter name and a JSON value; type_hint controls Variant deserialization (e.g. Vector2, Color, int, float). The value must match the shader's declared parameter type. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

material_rid.description: RID of the render material, from create_render_material

type_hint.description: Type hint (e.g. Vector2, Color, int, float)

value.description: Parameter value as JSON; plain numbers/strings/bools also work

tools.name: set_render_mesh_surface_material
tools.description: Assign a material to one surface of a mesh. Pass the RID from create_render_mesh, a 0-based surface index (in add_render_mesh_surface call order) and a material RID from create_render_material. Each surface can have its own material. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

material_rid.description: RID of the material to assign, from create_render_material

mesh_rid.description: RID of the render mesh, from create_render_mesh

surface.description: Surface index, 0-based in add_render_mesh_surface call order; example: 0 for the first surface

tools.name: set_render_particles_emitting
tools.description: Set whether a particle system is emitting. Pass the RID from create_render_particles; emitting defaults to true. To restart playback from the beginning, use restart_render_particles instead. Emitting alone does not restart a finished emission; combine with set_render_particles_lifetime to control duration. Returns 'ok'. Errors if particles_rid is missing.

emitting.description: Emit particles, true starts and false stops emission (default: true)

particles_rid.description: RID of the particle system, from create_render_particles

tools.name: set_render_particles_lifetime
tools.description: Set the lifetime of a particle system in seconds, controlling how long each emitted particle stays alive. Pass the RID from create_render_particles; lifetime defaults to 1.0. Pair with set_render_particles_emitting and restart_render_particles to control playback. Returns 'ok'. Errors if particles_rid is missing.

lifetime.description: Particle lifetime in seconds; controls how long each particle stays alive (default: 1.0)

particles_rid.description: RID of the particle system, from create_render_particles

tools.name: set_render_scenario_environment
tools.description: Attach an environment to a 3D scenario to drive background, ambient light, fog and post-processing. Pass the scenario RID from create_render_scenario; the environment RID must come from an external source (e.g. code_execute), as no create tool exists. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

environment_rid.description: RID of the environment to attach; must come from an external source (e.g. code_execute), as no create tool exists

scenario_rid.description: RID of the render scenario, from create_render_scenario

tools.name: set_render_shader_code
tools.description: Set the source code of a shader. Pass the RID from create_render_shader and the shader code as a string. It replaces any code set at creation time; compilation happens on the server side. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

code.description: Shader source code; must be a full shader file, not a snippet

shader_rid.description: RID of the shader, from create_render_shader

tools.name: set_render_shader_parameter_global
tools.description: Set a global shader parameter available to all shaders. The shader must declare a parameter with the same name using the global keyword. type_hint controls Variant deserialization (e.g. Vector2, Color, int, float). Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

name.description: Global shader parameter name; the shader must declare a matching parameter with the global keyword

type_hint.description: Type hint (e.g. Vector2, Color, int, float)

value.description: Parameter value as JSON; plain numbers/strings/bools also work

tools.name: set_render_sky_material
tools.description: Set the material of a sky. Pass the sky RID from create_render_sky and a material RID from create_render_material. The material defines the sky appearance, e.g. a procedural sky or panorama texture. Returns 'ok'. Errors if a required parameter is missing.

material_rid.description: RID of the material to assign, from create_render_material

sky_rid.description: RID of the sky, from create_render_sky

tools.name: set_render_viewport_clear_mode
tools.description: Set how a viewport clears its background each frame. Pass the RID from create_render_viewport; clear_mode is 0=always, 1=never, 2=only_next_frame and defaults to 0. Never clearing keeps the previous frame, useful for persistent drawing. Returns 'ok'. Errors if viewport_rid is missing.

viewport_rid.description: RID of the render viewport, from create_render_viewport

tools.name: set_render_viewport_size
tools.description: Set the pixel size of a viewport. Pass the RID from create_render_viewport; width defaults to 640 and height to 480. It determines the resolution of the viewport's render target. Change it at runtime to resize the target. Returns 'ok'. Errors if viewport_rid is missing.

viewport_rid.description: RID of the render viewport, from create_render_viewport

tools.name: set_resource_import_options
tools.description: Set whitelisted import options on an already-imported asset's .import [params] section and queue a reimport. Requires path (a res:// file that already carries a .import sidecar) and options (a non-empty object mapping option keys to values). Only safe importer keys are accepted (audio loop/compression and texture filter/mipmap families, e.g. loop, loop_mode, loop_begin, loop_end, compression, compress/mode, compress/high_quality, compress/lossy_quality, mipmaps/generate, mipmaps/limit, filter, anisotropy, process/hdr_as_srgb, roughness/mode, stream, size_limit); any other key is rejected. Do not hand-write .import files — this tool is the supported way to change import parameters. The reimport is asynchronous: the response reports applied keys with reimport queued, so poll get_editor_file_system_status until scanning is false, then verify with get_resource_type or read_file on the .import. Errors when the file has no .import sidecar (use reload_resource for plain text resources) or while the editor is importing/scanning.

options.description: Non-empty object mapping whitelisted importer option keys to new values (audio loop/compression and texture filter/mipmap families, e.g. loop, loop_begin, loop_end, compression, compress/mode, mipmaps/generate, filter); any other key is rejected

path.description: Imported asset path inside res:// that already carries a .import sidecar, e.g. res://assets/sfx/jump.wav; files without a sidecar are rejected

tools.name: set_resource_property
tools.description: Set a property on a resource. Locate the resource by object_id/object_id_str (from create_resource or load_resource), name (in-memory) or path (loaded from disk). value is a serialized JSON value; resource-typed properties accept {'path': 'res://...'} or {'resource': 'memory://name'} references, and type_hint guides deserialization. Returns ok with class, path, object_id, resource_attached and possible readback warnings.

name.description: Registration name of an in-memory resource (memory://name)

object_id.description: Object ID of an in-memory resource (from create_resource or load_resource)

object_id_str.description: Object ID as decimal string, alternative to object_id

path.description: Resource path; loads the file from disk when no object_id or name matches

property.description: Property name to set, e.g. curve, texture; must exist on the resource

type_hint.description: Variant type hint for deserialization, e.g. Vector2, Color, int, float; auto-detected from the property metadata when omitted

value.description: Serialized JSON value; resource-typed properties accept {'path': 'res://xxx.tres'} or {'resource': 'memory://name'} references

tools.name: set_resource_uid
tools.description: Assign a UID to a resource file so it can be referenced as uid://<id>, the counterpart of get_resource_uid. uid is optional: when omitted a fresh UID is auto-generated. Triggers a filesystem reimport so the assignment persists. Returns the UID that was applied.

path.description: Resource file path to assign the UID to, e.g. res://my_resource.tres

uid.description: UID value to assign; when omitted a fresh UID is auto-generated (contract gap: required in schema but optional in the implementation)

tools.name: set_scene_tree_debug_collisions_hint
tools.description: Act on the running game process's SceneTree over the runtime channel — requires a game launched from the editor whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension, and game_runtime authorization. Unlike editor scene tools, this never touches the editor's own scene tree: without a running game it returns a structured error. Toggle collision shape debug visualization in that game SceneTree. Requires 'enabled' (bool); sets the game's SceneTree debug collisions hint so collision shapes are drawn during gameplay. The hint only affects debug drawing, not physics behavior. Shapes render only while the game is running. Returns 'ok'.

enabled.description: Draw collision shapes while the scene runs (boolean, e.g. true)

tools.name: set_scene_tree_pause
tools.description: Act on the running game process's SceneTree over the runtime channel — requires a game launched from the editor whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension, and game_runtime authorization. Unlike editor scene tools, this never touches the editor's own scene tree: without a running game it returns a structured error, and the editor itself is never paused. Pause or unpause that game SceneTree. Requires 'paused' (bool). Only nodes whose process_mode permits WhenPaused keep processing while paused; process and physics callbacks of other nodes are not called. Query the resulting state with is_scene_tree_paused. Pass 'paused': false to resume the game. Returns result true.

paused.description: Pause state: true pauses the scene tree, false resumes (boolean)

tools.name: set_script_property
tools.description: Set a property directly on a node: a lightweight alternative to property_set with no undo entry and no type or read-only validation. Requires node_path, property and value; optional type_hint helps deserialize JSON into the right Variant type. Use property_set when undo support and validation matter; use this tool for quick in-memory tweaks that must not touch the undo stack.

node_path.description: Node path in the edited scene

value.description: Property value as JSON; the tool performs no type or read-only validation and creates no undo entry — use property_set for validated, undoable changes

tools.name: set_text_font_antialiasing
tools.description: Set the antialiasing mode of a font created by create_text_font. Requires font_rid (the RID id returned by create_text_font) and antialiasing (0=none, 1=gray, 2=grayscale, 3=subpixel). Call after set_text_font_data so the mode applies to the loaded font. Use 0 for pixel-art fonts. Returns 'ok'.

tools.name: set_text_font_data
tools.description: Load a font file and assign its bytes to a font created by create_text_font. 'data' is a path to a font file (.ttf, .otf, .woff2); get_text_font_system_path returns an absolute path that can be passed here directly. Requires font_rid from create_text_font. Returns 'ok'; errors when the file cannot be read.

data.description: Path to a font file (.ttf, .otf, .woff2); get_text_font_system_path returns a usable path

tools.name: set_text_font_hinting
tools.description: Set the hinting mode of a font created by create_text_font. Requires font_rid (the RID id returned by create_text_font) and hinting (0=none, 1=light, 2=normal). Apply after set_text_font_data so the setting affects the loaded font. Light hinting is the typical default for UI text. Returns 'ok'.

tools.name: set_theme_color
tools.description: Set a color item on a saved .tres theme. Requires path, theme_type (the widget class the item belongs to, e.g. Button or Label) and varname (the item name, e.g. font_color); color accepts a hex string like "#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa" or an object {r,g,b,a} with floats in 0..1. The theme is loaded, modified and saved back to disk. Use get_theme_info to discover valid type/name pairs. Returns ok with saved:true.

color.description: Color value: hex string like '#rrggbb' or '#rrggbbaa', or object {r,g,b,a} with floats in 0..1

path.description: Path of a saved .tres theme file created with create_theme_resource

theme_type.description: Widget class the color item belongs to, e.g. 'Button' or 'Label'

tools.name: set_theme_constant
tools.description: Set an integer constant item (e.g. separation, outline_size) on a saved .tres theme. Requires path, theme_type and varname plus the integer constant. The theme is loaded, modified and saved back to disk. Returns ok with saved:true.

path.description: Path of a saved .tres theme file created with create_theme_resource

theme_type.description: Widget class the constant item belongs to, e.g. 'Button'

tools.name: set_theme_font_size
tools.description: Set a font size item on a saved .tres theme. Requires path, theme_type and varname plus the integer font_size. The theme is loaded, modified and saved back to disk; use set_theme_color or set_theme_stylebox_flat for other item kinds. Returns ok with saved:true.

font_size.description: Integer font size value to set

path.description: Path of a saved .tres theme file created with create_theme_resource

theme_type.description: Widget class the font size item belongs to, e.g. 'Label'

tools.name: set_theme_item_bundle
tools.description: Set many theme items on a saved .tres theme in one save. Requires path plus at least one of colors, constants, font_sizes or styleboxes, each mapping theme_type to {varname: value} objects. Colors accept hex strings like "#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa" or objects {r,g,b,a} with floats in 0..1; constants and font_sizes take integers; styleboxes take StyleBoxFlat definitions with the same fields as set_theme_stylebox_flat. The theme is loaded, all items are modified in memory and saved back to disk once with a reload verification. Use get_theme_info to discover valid type and name pairs. Returns ok with per-kind applied counts plus saved and verified.

colors.description: Color items as object mapping theme_type to {varname: color} objects, e.g. {'Button': {'font_color': '#ff0000'}}; each color accepts a hex string like '#rrggbb' or '#rrggbbaa' or an object {r,g,b,a} with floats in 0..1

constants.description: Constant items as object mapping theme_type to {varname: integer} objects, e.g. {'Button': {'separation': 4}}

font_sizes.description: Font size items as object mapping theme_type to {varname: integer} objects, e.g. {'Label': {'font_size': 16}}

path.description: Path of a saved .tres theme file created with create_theme_resource, e.g. 'res://themes/main.tres'

styleboxes.description: Stylebox items as object mapping theme_type to {varname: stylebox} objects, e.g. {'Button': {'normal': {'bg_color': '#202020'}}}; each stylebox holds optional bg_color and border_color (hex string or {r,g,b,a}), border_width {left,top,right,bottom}, corner_radius {top_left,top_right,bottom_right,bottom_left} and content_margin {left,top,right,bottom} — every field is optional, and border_width/content_margin also accept a single number applied to all sides

tools.name: set_theme_stylebox_flat
tools.description: Build a StyleBoxFlat and register it as the stylebox item varname under theme_type of a saved .tres theme. The stylebox object holds optional bg_color and border_color (hex string or {r,g,b,a}), border_width {left,top,right,bottom}, corner_radius {top_left,top_right,bottom_right,bottom_left} and content_margin {left,top,right,bottom} — every field is optional, and border_width/content_margin also accept a single number applied to all sides. The theme is loaded, modified and saved back to disk. Returns ok with saved:true.

path.description: Path of a saved .tres theme file created with create_theme_resource

stylebox.description: StyleBoxFlat definition: optional bg_color/border_color (hex string or {r,g,b,a}), border_width {left,top,right,bottom}, corner_radius {top_left,top_right,bottom_right,bottom_left}, content_margin {left,top,right,bottom}; border_width/content_margin also accept a single number applied to all sides

theme_type.description: Widget class the stylebox item belongs to, e.g. 'Button'

tools.name: set_tilemap_cell
tools.description: Set a single cell on a TileMap or TileMapLayer node. Requires path, x, y; optional layer (default 0), source_id (default 0) and atlas_coords {x, y} place the tile. The source must exist in the node's TileSet (build it with create_tilemap_tileset + add_tilemap_atlas_source first). Passing source_id -1 clears the cell at x, y instead (atlas_coords is ignored then). Returns 'ok'; use set_tilemap_cells for batches.

layer.description: Tile layer index (default: 0); TileMapLayer nodes ignore it

path.description: Path to the TileMap or TileMapLayer node

source_id.description: TileSet source ID (default: 0); must exist in the node's TileSet

tools.name: set_tilemap_cells
tools.description: Set multiple cells on a TileMap or TileMapLayer node in one call. Every entry must be an object with x, y and source_id (atlas_coords optional); an entry with source_id -1 clears the cell at x, y (atlas_coords is ignored for that entry). Invalid entries are skipped and reported via error plus warnings. Returns set_count and layer. There is no fixed entry cap, but keep batches reasonably sized because client-side request limits may apply; generate big layouts programmatically with execute_script or code_execute instead.

cells.description: Array of cells, each {"x":int,"y":int,"source_id":int,"atlas_coords":{"x":int,"y":int}} — source_id is required per entry. No fixed server-side entry cap, but keep batches reasonably sized because client or transport layers may limit a single request payload (bigger layouts: loop in execute_script or code_execute). An entry with source_id -1 clears the cell at x, y (atlas_coords is ignored and may be omitted). Invalid entries are skipped and reported in the error plus warnings

layer.description: Tile layer index (default: 0); TileMapLayer nodes ignore it

node_path.description: Path to the TileMap or TileMapLayer node

tools.name: set_tilemap_tile_collision
tools.description: Set collision polygons for one tile of a TileSet. Requires name (memory:// TileSet reference), source_id, atlas_coords and physics_layer; the TileSet needs an atlas source and a physics layer first (create_tilemap_tileset → add_tilemap_atlas_source → add_tilemap_physics_layer). polygon is an array of {x, y} points or an array of such arrays for multiple polygons; an empty array clears existing collision. Points are relative to the tile center. Returns 'ok', atlas_coords and polygon_points.

name.description: TileSet name from create_tilemap_tileset (memory:// reference)

physics_layer.description: Physics layer index added by add_tilemap_physics_layer

polygon.description: Collision polygon: array of {x,y} points, or array of such arrays for multiple polygons; an empty array clears existing collision. Points are relative to the TILE CENTER (e.g. for tile_size=16 use (-8,-8)-(8,8) for full-tile collision; (0,0)-(16,16) starts at the center and overhangs)

source_id.description: Source ID of the atlas source added by add_tilemap_atlas_source

tools.name: show_display_dialog
tools.description: Show a native modal dialog with a title, description and the given button labels using the operating system. Use it to prompt the user or surface a message outside the editor UI. Takes title, description and an array of button label strings. The dialog is fire-and-forget: an empty callback is passed, so the clicked button cannot be reported back to the caller.

buttons.description: Array of button label strings, one button per entry, e.g. ['OK', 'Cancel']; note the dialog is fire-and-forget, so the clicked button is not reported back

description.description: Message body shown inside the dialog

title.description: Title shown in the dialog's title bar

tools.name: show_os_alert
tools.description: Ask the editor to show an alert to the user. By default the call does NOT open a dialog: it returns a structured notice (shown=false, requires_confirmation=true) carrying the text and title and explaining that the alert needs human confirmation. A modal alert blocks the editor main thread until the user dismisses it, so unattended or automated runs would hang — only pass modal=true when a human is watching the editor. Requires 'text' (string); optional 'title' (default: Alert!) and 'modal' (boolean, default false). Returns result 'ok' plus shown.

modal.description: Actually open the modal dialog (default: false). With false the call returns a structured notice (shown=false, requires_confirmation=true) instead of a dialog, because a modal alert blocks the editor main thread until a human dismisses it and freezes unattended runs. Set true only when a human is watching the editor

text.description: Message to show in the alert body; it is only displayed when modal=true, otherwise it is returned as part of the confirmation notice

tools.name: signal_connect
tools.description: Connect a signal on 'source_path' to a method on 'target_path'; requires 'source_path', 'signal', 'target_path', 'method'. 'persist' (default true) uses CONNECT_PERSIST, saving the connection with the scene and making every instantiation inherit it; set false for a runtime-only connection that is not saved. Returns 'connected', or 'already_connected' when the pair already exists (use signal_disconnect to remove it), plus 'persisted' and a note.

method.description: Method name to call on the target node (string, e.g. 'set_health')

persist.description: Persist the connection with CONNECT_PERSIST so it is saved with the scene and inherited by instantiations (boolean, default: true); false creates a runtime-only connection that is not saved

signal.description: Signal name on the source node (string, e.g. 'health_changed')

source_path.description: Node path of the signal emitter (string, e.g. 'Player')

target_path.description: Node path of the receiver (string, e.g. 'UI/HealthBar')

tools.name: signal_disconnect
tools.description: Remove a signal connection previously created by signal_connect. Requires the same four parameters: 'source_path', 'signal', 'target_path', 'method'. Returns 'disconnected', or 'not_connected' when the signal+callable pair does not exist (idempotent — repeated calls are safe). Persistent connections removed here stop being saved with the scene.

method.description: Method name of the connected callable (string, e.g. 'set_health')

signal.description: Signal name on the source node (string, e.g. 'health_changed')

source_path.description: Node path of the signal emitter (string, e.g. 'Player')

target_path.description: Node path of the receiver (string, e.g. 'UI/HealthBar')

tools.name: spawn_node_bundle
tools.description: Create one node and finish its common setup in a single atomic call: 'type' (any Node subclass, default Node) and 'name' (default Node, '/' and ':' rejected) under 'parent_path' (default: edited scene root; omit only while the scene has no root, in which case the new node becomes the root). Optional 'properties' object is applied via set_properties_batch with atomic:true, optional 'script_path' (must start with 'res://') is attached via attach_script_to_node with a fresh disk re-read, optional 'groups' (array of 1..16 names) is added persistently via add_group_node with editor undo registration, and optional 'connections' (array of {signal, target_path, method, persist} with persist defaulting to true for CONNECT_PERSIST scene-saved wiring) is connected from the new node via signal_connect. Optional 'owner' (default true) keeps scene ownership so the node is saved; 'dry_run'/'preview' (either true) only validates and previews without writing. The steps run in order properties, script, groups, connections; any failing step removes the new node and rolls the whole bundle back with no residue. Returns the new node 'path' and 'type', the 'applied' property name array, 'groups_connected' and 'signals_connected' counts, and an 'undo' hint describing how to remove the node via delete_scene_node.

connections.description: Optional array of {signal, target_path, method, persist} objects connected from the new node via signal_connect; persist defaults to true (CONNECT_PERSIST, saved with the scene)

dry_run.description: Validate parameters and return the preview without writing to the scene (default: false); either dry_run or preview enables preview-only mode

groups.description: Optional array of 1..16 group names added persistently via add_group_node with editor undo registration

name.description: Node name (string, default: Node); '/' and ':' are rejected

owner.description: Set scene ownership so the node is saved with the scene (boolean, default: true)

parent_path.description: Parent node path in the edited scene (string, default: edited scene root); omit only while the scene has no root, in which case the new node becomes the root

preview.description: Alias of dry_run: validate and preview without writing (default: false)

properties.description: Optional map of property names to values applied via set_properties_batch with atomic:true (object, e.g. {"visible": false}); any failing property rolls the whole bundle back

script_path.description: Optional Script resource path to attach via attach_script_to_node (string, must start with 'res://'); the script is re-read from disk before attaching

type.description: Node class type (string, default: Node). Must be a Node subclass, e.g. Node2D, Sprite2D — other classes error

tools.name: speak_display_tts
tools.description: Speak the given text aloud using the system text-to-speech engine. Use it for accessibility or audible feedback in the project. Optionally pass a voice id from get_display_tts_voices, volume 0-100 (default 50), pitch (default 1.0) and rate (default 1.0). Speech is asynchronous; interrupt it with stop_display_tts. Returns result 'ok'.

pitch.description: Speech pitch multiplier, default 1.0; values above 1.0 raise the pitch

rate.description: Speech speed multiplier, default 1.0; values above 1.0 speak faster

text.description: Text to synthesize and speak aloud, e.g. 'Level complete'

voice.description: Voice id from get_display_tts_voices; omit to use the system default voice

tools.name: start_audio_input_capture
tools.description: Start capturing audio from the input device into the AudioServer input buffer. Optionally pass 'device' (a name from get_audio_input_devices) to select the device first, otherwise the current device keeps being used. Pair with stop_audio_input_capture, which drains the buffer into a memory WAV. Returns 'result' set to 'ok'.

device.description: Optional input device name as returned by get_audio_input_devices; when given, the device is selected before capture starts, otherwise the current device keeps being used

tools.name: start_game_job
tools.description: Submit a game op for asynchronous execution inside the running game process over the runtime debug channel and return immediately with a job_id instead of waiting for the result; submit without waiting, poll with get_game_job. Use it for long-running scripts that would exceed the 25 s per-call timeout budget. op is currently 'eval' only and params carries that op's parameters verbatim (same fields as execute_game_script, e.g. {"action":"script","source_code":"..."}); timeout_ms (default 5000, max 25000) bounds the in-game execution and the job expiry check, not the submit call. The job table holds at most 16 jobs and entries expire timeout_ms + 2000 ms after start. Requires a game launched from the editor whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension and the game_runtime authorization gate.

op.description: Wrapped game op to submit for asynchronous execution; currently only 'eval' (the execute_game_script op) is supported

params.description: Parameters object passed to the wrapped op verbatim — same fields as execute_game_script, e.g. {"action":"script","source_code":"..."}

timeout_ms.description: In-game execution budget in milliseconds (default: 5000, maximum: 25000); the call returns immediately with a job_id and does not wait, so this bounds the in-game run and the job expiry check (expiry at timeout_ms + 2000 ms) instead of the transport wait. The job table holds at most 16 entries — collect finished jobs with get_game_job to free slots. Same budget chain as execute_game_script: values above 25000 are rejected, keeping every host wait below the 30 s HTTP transport timeout

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready (gda:ready) before failing; while the game is starting, the request is queued and replayed as soon as readiness arrives. Set false to fail immediately (previous behaviour). Default: true

tools.name: start_input_gamepad_vibration
tools.description: Start vibration on a gamepad connected to the editor process. 'device' is the gamepad index and defaults to 0; 'weak' and 'strong' set the two motor magnitudes from 0.0 to 1.0 and default to 0.5. 'duration' is in seconds and defaults to 0, which vibrates indefinitely until stop_input_gamepad_vibration is called. A running game is a separate process and is not affected.

duration.description: Vibration duration in seconds; 0 (default) vibrates indefinitely until stop_input_gamepad_vibration

tools.name: stop_audio_input_capture
tools.description: Stop input capture and drain the buffered frames into a new AudioStreamWAV registered as 'memory://name'. 'name' is required; 'format' accepts 8 or 16 (default 16) and any other value is rejected; 'mix_rate' defaults to the current input mix rate; 'stereo' false keeps the left channel only while true interleaves both channels; 'max_frames' drains at most that many frames (default: all available). When more than 1000000 frames are requested only the first 1000000 are kept and 'truncated' is set to true. Returns the WAV locator with format, mix_rate, stereo, frames and truncated in 'result'. Save it to disk before assigning it to a node property.

format.description: Sample format in bits; 8 or 16 (default 16); any other value is rejected

max_frames.description: Maximum frames to drain from the input buffer (default: all available); must be at least 1; captures longer than 1000000 frames keep only the first 1000000 and report truncated true

mix_rate.description: Mix rate in Hz stored on the WAV (default: current input mix rate); must be an integer in 1000..192000

name.description: Registration name for the captured take; the resulting AudioStreamWAV stays alive as 'memory://name' for later tools

stereo.description: Capture both channels interleaved when true (default false keeps the left channel only)

tools.name: stop_audio_player
tools.description: Stop playback on an AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStreamPlayer2D or AudioStreamPlayer3D node. 'node_path' is a scene-relative path such as 'Level1/Player' or an absolute '/root/...' path. The stream stays assigned, so the node can be played again with play_audio_player. Returns 'result' set to 'ok'.

node_path.description: Scene-relative path to an AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStreamPlayer2D or AudioStreamPlayer3D node, e.g. 'Level1/Player' or absolute '/root/Level1/Player'

tools.name: stop_display_tts
tools.description: Stop any ongoing text-to-speech playback immediately. Use it to interrupt speech started with speak_display_tts, e.g. when new text should be spoken or the user is done listening. Returns result 'ok' even when nothing is currently being spoken, making it safe to call unconditionally.

tools.name: stop_editor_playing
tools.description: Stop the running game process started by play_editor_current_scene and return the editor to editing mode. Use it at the end of a play-testing session or before modifying the scene again. Returns result 'ok' even when no game is currently running.

tools.name: stop_input_gamepad_vibration
tools.description: Stop vibration on a gamepad connected to the editor process, ending any vibration started with start_input_gamepad_vibration. 'device' is the gamepad index and defaults to 0. A running game is a separate process and is not affected. Returns 'result' set to 'ok'.

tools.name: system_status
tools.description: Get server status info

tools.name: trace_signal_flow
tools.description: Trace signal wiring around a node of the edited scene. Required 'path' (string, scene-relative node path, e.g. "Player"); optional 'direction' (string: "outgoing" for signals the node emits, "incoming" for connections targeting it, default "both") and 'max_depth' (int >= 1, how many hops to walk from the start node, default 3; cycles are cut by a visited set). Each edge is {from,signal,to,method,persisted} where 'persisted' marks connections saved in the scene file (CONNECT_PERSIST). Non-node targets such as autoloads are shown as Class#instance_id. Returns {root, edges, edge_count}.

direction.description: Which connections to report: 'outgoing' (signals the node emits), 'incoming' (connections targeting it) or 'both' (default)

max_depth.description: How many hops to walk from the start node, >= 1 (default: 3); cycles are cut by a visited set

path.description: Scene-relative node path of the node whose signal wiring is traced (e.g. "Player")

tools.name: translate_text
tools.description: Translate a message key with the TranslationServer singleton under the current game locale (see get_game_locale). Requires key (non-empty source message); unknown keys fail with an error instead of echoing the key. Returns the translated string plus the resolving key and locale.

key.description: Source message key to translate under the current game locale; unknown keys fail instead of echoing the key

tools.name: tween_editor_property
tools.description: Preview a property tween on a node of the currently edited scene without running the game: pass path (node path in the edited scene) and property plus target_value (converted with the property_set chain) and duration (seconds, greater than 0). The tween is created straight on the editor SceneTree via SceneTree::create_tween and its int64 handle is kept in the editor-side TweenStore for the session; optional trans (0-10), ease (0-3) and loops (>= 0, 0 means infinite) shape the playback. Returns tween_id with scene_path and scene_unsaved so the caller can confirm which scene the preview node belongs to.

duration.description: Tween duration in seconds for one loop (number greater than 0)

loops.description: Loop count, an integer >= 0 (0 means infinite loop; default 1)

path.description: Node path in the edited scene (e.g. 'Player/Sprite2D'). The response includes scene_path and scene_unsaved to confirm which scene the preview node belongs to

property.description: Property to animate, e.g. position, scale or modulate:a; must exist on the node or the call fails fast

target_value.description: Final value the property animates to, converted with the same chain as property_set (e.g. {"x": 10, "y": 20} for a Vector2, a plain number for scalar properties)

tools.name: type_editor_element_text
tools.description: Focus an editor UI element and write text into it by pushing the whole string as one text-input event instead of simulating keystrokes. Use it to fill editor fields such as search boxes or property inputs resolved through get_editor_ui_elements; the element is focused with grab_focus when it does not already have focus. Optional 'submit' (default false) appends an Enter press and release. Optional 'observe' (default false) appends a fresh editor viewport capture to the result. Returns result with ok, path, length, focused and submit. Editor process only.

observe.description: Append a fresh editor viewport capture to the result (default: false)

path.description: Element path as returned by get_editor_ui_elements or hit_test_editor_point

submit.description: Append an Enter key press and release after the text (default: false)

text.description: Text to write into the focused element; may contain any UTF-8 text

tools.name: type_input_text
tools.description: Write text into the control that currently has keyboard focus in the editor process by pushing the whole string as one text-input event, not by simulating individual key presses. Focus the target first with click_input_mouse or click_editor_element; typing while a dock has no focus does nothing. 'text' is required and may contain any UTF-8 text; 'submit' (default false) appends an Enter key press and release, e.g. to confirm a LineEdit. Optional 'observe' (default false) appends a fresh editor viewport capture to the result. A running game is a separate process and will not receive this input. Returns result with ok true and 'length', the number of characters written.

observe.description: Append a fresh editor viewport capture to the result (default: false)

submit.description: Append an Enter key press and release after the text (default: false)

text.description: Text to write into the focused control; may contain any UTF-8 text

tools.name: validate_game_ui_layout
tools.description: Scan the running game's Control tree for layout defects, read-only: zero-size visible controls, controls fully outside the viewport visible rect and possibly-occluded controls, each reported as {kind,severity,path,type,rect,detail}. Requires a game launched from the editor whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension. Invisible controls are always skipped; ignore_paths (up to 50 exact or '/'-suffix paths) and ignore_classes (up to 20 class names, subclasses match, e.g. 'Container' covers layout-only containers) suppress known-good entries. Thresholds guard against false positives: min_area (default 4.0, smaller visible areas report tiny_area info), bounds_margin (default 2.0 px tolerance around the viewport), occlude_ratio (0.5-1.0, default 0.98 — fraction of an element's area covered by a later visible control before possibly_occluded warns; controls are compared in effective z_index order — each control's z_index accumulated up its ancestors while z_as_relative holds — then document order, and a control with mouse_filter=IGNORE never counts as an occluder). Possibly-occluded entries also carry occluder_path and occluder_mouse_filter (the covering control and its STOP/PASS/IGNORE filter), and the response adds possibly_occluded_count as a scalar total of the possibly_occluded entries emitted. max_elements caps the enumeration (default 100, max 1000); truncated=true signals more remain. No automatic verdict — triage the issues yourself.

bounds_margin.description: Pixel tolerance around the viewport visible rect (default: 2.0)

ignore_classes.description: Up to 20 class names suppressing known-good entries; subclasses match, e.g. Container covers layout-only containers

ignore_paths.description: Up to 50 exact or '/'-suffix paths suppressing known-good entries

max_elements.description: Maximum number of Control elements enumerated (default: 100); truncated=true signals more remain

min_area.description: Visible areas below this size report tiny_area info (default: 4.0)

occlude_ratio.description: Fraction 0.5-1.0 of an element area covered by a later visible control before possibly_occluded warns (default: 0.98); controls are compared in effective z_index order then document order, and controls with mouse_filter=IGNORE never count as occluders

timeout_ms.description: Response timeout in milliseconds (default: 5000, max: 25000). The host waits timeout_ms + 2000 ms and that budget must stay below the 30 s HTTP transport timeout, so 25000 ms is the hard cap

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready (gda:ready) before failing; while the game is starting, the request is queued and replayed as soon as readiness arrives. Set false to fail immediately (previous behaviour). Default: true

tools.name: validate_scene_file
tools.description: Dry-run validate a scene file on disk without touching the currently edited scene. Required 'path' (string, res:// path to a .tscn/.scn file, e.g. "res://levels/level_01.tscn"). Loads it via ResourceLoader with CACHE_MODE_IGNORE (bypasses the resource cache), checks every dependency reported by get_dependencies for existence on disk, then calls PackedScene::instantiate() and immediately frees the instance. Returns {valid, problems:[{kind,message}], missing_dependencies, dependency_count}; problem kinds: load_failed / missing_dependency / instantiate_failed. Use after bulk edits or before committing scene changes.

path.description: res:// path to a .tscn/.scn scene file on disk to dry-run validate (e.g. "res://levels/level_01.tscn"); loaded with CACHE_MODE_IGNORE, dependencies checked and instantiate() attempted without touching the edited scene

tools.name: verify_scene_saved
tools.description: Compare the in-memory edited scene tree against its on-disk .tscn file without modifying anything. Use it after save_editor_scene or save_editor_scene_as to prove the save persisted every node (e.g. after moving a subtree with children), or as a standalone consistency check. Returns result 'match' or 'mismatch' plus memory_nodes, disk_nodes, match, missing_paths (memory paths absent on disk, capped at 50 with missing_truncated) and path; optional scene_path overrides the compared file, include_hash adds FNV-1a memory_hash/disk_hash. inherited_nodes and inherited_connections count the nodes and connections inside sub-scene instances that are never written to the .tscn, inherited_paths lists those node paths when any exist (capped at 50 with inherited_truncated), and the match verdict compares only the persistable node and connection set. Read-only.

include_hash.description: Attach FNV-1a content hashes of the memory tree and the on-disk file (memory_hash/disk_hash); off by default

scene_path.description: Scene file path to compare against the in-memory tree, e.g. 'res://game.tscn'; when omitted the current scene file path is used

tools.name: wait_game_input
tools.description: Wait for a transient input state on an action in the running game process over the runtime debug channel; requires a game launched from the editor whose project loads the godot-autopilot extension. state is 'just_pressed' (default), 'just_released' or 'pressed'; the call returns when the state is observed in a physics frame or timeout_ms elapses (default 2000, max 25000; the host waits timeout_ms + 2000 ms, below the 30 s transport timeout). Optional inject sends input first in the same call, avoiding frame skew between round trips; state=just_pressed/just_released requires inject — without it the 1-frame transient window has already expired and the wait always times out. Transient states are tracked against physics frames only: is_action_just_pressed polled in _process (render frame) will not observe injected input — poll in _physics_process instead.

inject.description: Inject an input before waiting, in the same call (fields mirror queue_game_input: type/action/keycode/pressed/mode/duration_ms/button_index/position/direction/amount/relative/click/double_click) — eliminates the inject-then-observe cross-roundtrip frame gap; required for state=just_pressed/just_released, without inject the transient window (1 physics frame) has already expired and the wait will always time out. Transient states are not visible in _process (render frame)

state.description: Transient state to wait for: 'just_pressed' (default), 'just_released' or 'pressed'

timeout_ms.description: Wait timeout in milliseconds (default: 2000, max: 25000). The host waits timeout_ms + 2000 ms and that budget must stay below the 30 s HTTP transport timeout, so 25000 ms is the hard cap — split long work into shorter calls

wait_ready.description: Wait for the game process to report ready (gda:ready) before failing; while the game is starting, the request is queued and replayed as soon as readiness arrives. Set false to fail immediately (previous behaviour). Default: true

tools.name: warp_display_mouse
tools.description: Move the mouse cursor instantly to the given position, in pixels relative to the client area of the focused window — the engine converts the position onto the desktop — not screen coordinates, and not the basis reported by get_display_mouse_position. Use it to place the pointer before simulating clicks with the input tools, e.g. warp_display_mouse to the target, then move_input_mouse and press_input_mouse_button at the same window-client coordinates. Takes integer x and y. Returns result 'ok'; behavior may vary slightly between platforms.

x.description: Mouse X position in pixels relative to the client area of the focused window (not screen coordinates), e.g. 640

y.description: Mouse Y position in pixels relative to the client area of the focused window (not screen coordinates), e.g. 360

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write or append text content to a file. Paths inside the project (res://) are engine-managed: after writing, the file is synced with the editor file system — imported asset types (images, audio, fonts, 3D models, translations, or any file that already has a .import sidecar) are queued for reimport while plain text files get update_file; script-like files (.gd/.gdshader/.gdshaderinc/.cs) additionally return a diagnostics object. diagnostics.ok is not a blanket success flag: for .gd it is true only when the written source passes the compiler gate (diagnostic_scope=compile, compilable=true/false; a compile failure returns ok=false with parse_error{line,message} while the file stays on disk — fix the reported line and write it again), for .gdshader/.gdshaderinc only resource load is checked (diagnostic_scope=load, compilable=unknown), and for .cs the editor cannot compile the file at all (diagnostic_scope=resource_load, compilable=unknown, assembly_checked reports whether the .NET assembly is currently loaded, with is_dotnet_editor/assembly_loaded describing the editor state) — confirm C# compilation with build_csharp_assembly and read get_debugger_log for its errors. diagnostics.instantiable is reported when the resource loads and reflects whether the editor can instantiate it. External paths (user:// or absolute) are written as plain I/O outside editor tracking and report engine_managed: false. Requires 'path' and 'content' (strings); optional 'mode' is 'WRITE' (overwrite, default) or 'APPEND' (the resulting full file is compiled, not just the appended text). Returns result 'ok', plus engine_managed and action ('reimport' or 'update_file') for managed writes.

content.description: Text content to store in the file

mode.description: Write mode: 'WRITE' overwrites existing content (default), 'APPEND' appends to the end of the file

path.description: File path to write; res:// paths are engine-managed (automatic reimport/update_file sync and script diagnostics), user:// or absolute paths are plain I/O

tools.name: batch_execute
tools.description: Execute multiple tools in batch. Each operation runs in sequence; if stop_on_error is true and any operation fails, remaining operations are skipped. Async game tools are refused unless await_async=true, in which case batch_execute waits for the game response and reports it under result. With stop_on_error=true and rollback_on_error=true the changes of already-executed operations are rolled back through the global undo history when the batch stops.

await_async.description: Wait for async game ops instead of refusing them (default: false). With false an async game op is reported as an error telling you to use call_tool or await_async=true; with true batch_execute waits for the game response (bounded by the op's timeout_ms) and reports ok/error per response under result

operations.description: Ordered list of operations to execute; each result carries status 'ok'/'error'. An async game op (execute_game_script, queue_game_input, wait_game_input, sequence_game_inputs, get_game_ui_elements, click_game_ui_element, capture_game_viewport, capture_editor_viewport with target='game') is refused with status 'error' unless await_async=true; its pending record is always released. Response counts: 'total' = executed operations (succeeded+failed), 'skipped' = operations not run after stop_on_error truncation

rollback_on_error.description: Only effective when stop_on_error is true; when the batch stops on an error the changes of already-executed operations are rolled back through the global undo history; the response carries rolled_back and rollback_partial; changes that never entered the global undo history are not rolled back

tools.name: call_tool
tools.description: Execute any tool by name. Use this to call all 452 non-meta tools (451 domain tools plus system_status).

name.description: Tool name to execute

tools.name: code_execute
tools.description: Execute arbitrary GDScript code. The source code is wrapped in a script that extends Node, compiled, attached to a temporary node, and executed. Returns the function result serialized as JSON. Without a line-start `func ` definition the source is inlined inside the entry-function body: write straight-line code ending in return. When any non-comment line starts with `func ` (leading spaces/tabs stripped; `#` and `//` comment lines ignored) the whole source is preserved verbatim and function_name (default _run) selects the entry point, with a `func <name>(): pass` stub appended when the named entry is missing. Detection needs `func ` with a trailing space: `func<TAB>name():` or `func(` do not switch modes and are rejected in single-function mode; mixing tab and space indentation is rejected. Execution environment exposes SceneRoot (the edited scene root node) for node access; see SceneRoot.get_node("Child").

auto_owner.description: Automatically set owner on nodes created during execution so they are saved with the scene (default true)

timeout_ms.description: Execution timeout in milliseconds (max 27000)

tools.name: get_tool_detail
tools.description: Get complete schema for one tool

name.description: Tool name (e.g. ping, search_tools)

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: List all tool categories

tools.name: ping
tools.description: Health check ping

tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Search available tools by query

query.description: Search query; omit or pass an empty string to enumerate all tools
